items.body:
The previous Ezz-thetics column reflected the near-simultaneous appearance of three works of individual brilliance, solo recordings by Liz Allbee, Hannah Marshall, and John Butcher. In the months since, three mid-size, improvisation-rich ensembles, drawing inspiration from more or less explicit environmental themes have appeared, with varying degrees of composition and improvisation, led by musicians of comparable vision: Magda Mayas, Pascal Niggenkemper, and Marta Warelis.

Each is characterized by different degrees of copyright participation, signalling contrasting relations of composition and improvisation. Magda Mayas' Filamental's Murmur, evidently as collective as a murmuration of starlings, is copyrighted in the names of all eight musicians. Pascal Niggenkemper's d'une rive a l'autre is largely copyrighted to the composer/bassist, 11 of the 17 tracks, with six tracks credited to improvised duets from the eight instrumentalists of the Ensemble Tuvalu. Marta Warelis's Still Life with Lemons is largely credited to the leader/composer. All recently released, the three come from a specific moment in time, the autumn of 2024: Murmur was recorded in Berlin in September; Still Life with Lemons in Amsterdam in October; d'une rive a l'autre in Berlin in November.

Magda Mayas' Filamental's Murmur (Relative Pitch) is an octet with a strong emphasis on strings in its make-up; as well as the leader's piano, there are two harpists, Zeena Parkins and Rhodri Davies, pretty much covering the terrain of free improvising harpists; two cellists, Aimee Theriot-Ramos and Anthea Caddy; two reeds, alto saxophonist Christine Abdelnour and clarinetist Michael Thieke, and violinist Angharad Davies. Murmur is a singular piece, almost 38 minutes long.

There are few spectacles as emblematic of collective mind as a murmuration of starlings, thousands of birds joined in extraordinary aerobatic maneuvers that mock the reckless waste, noise, and danger of fighter jet ballets. Part of the special genius of Magda Mayas' Filamental is that it never sounds anything like what one might expect from its string-heavy personnel. Everything is sublimated into quiet percussive events, a music that suggests the sublime piety of chance events in nature, like a light rain on large leaves. Hence, Mayas' description of the work:

I am fascinated by the coordination and elegance of a flock of birds flying, forming beautiful murmurations, constantly changing, seemingly without effort. This communal act provides protection through the sheer number of birds and their changing position; it is an exchange of information amongst them, and it has a clear collective ending when the flock decides to fly back to the ground.

In Murmur, I want to explore how a large ensemble can make use of these instincts of communal movement, coordination, shape shifting and, eventually, potential simultaneous endings through distinct decisions around material and structure but also shared memories of events that were created together.

The doubling of instruments will lend a certain anonymity to the music, furthered by the frequency of isolated percussive details, whether a sustained note from Abdenour suggests a bowed string instrument, or cellos and/or violin are used for a maze of quarter tones. It's the very nature of the murmuration that will define this collective composition, hive mind or flock consciousness, yes, some overriding shared awareness, existence, and impulse. With no dedicated percussionist present (depending on how you might classify the piano), this is frequently percussion music of the highest order, struck strings on piano and string instruments create a bevy of string-drum plosives. The collective act itself is essentially harmonious in its nature, the special transparency of string harmonics creating a sonic window that opens onto the Cagean silence of the entire ensemble. The cumulative experience is of an interior soundscape in art channeled through the piano and taking place both in the octet and in the listener. A rare and beautiful sonic act.

Pascal Niggenkemper's Ensemble Tuvalu's d'une rive a l'autre (Subran 07) is inspired by Tuvalu, the Polynesian archipelago that is currently set to disappear below the Pacific's waves in a few decades, a paradisical world doomed by climate change. As with Mayas' Murmur, the bassist/composer's ensemble is an octet, made up of instrumental pairings: Ben LaMar Gay's cornet with Louis Lorain's trumpet; Mona Matbou Riahi's clarinet with Joachim Badenhorst's; Tizia Zimmermann's accordion with that of Artemis Vavatsika's; Niggenkemper's double bass paired, less precisely, with Elisabeth Coudoux's cello. Each of the musicians will also have a vocal role, singing, chanting, or reciting, and Jaumes Privat will appear near the end of the work for an extended spoken word passage.

In her expansive liner note, Julia Neupert, cites the composer's overarching concerns here:

Niggenkemper is interested in how differently people are shaped - culturally, socially, emotionally - not only in musical terms. He is concerned with broadening perspectives, recognizing other points of view, and collective thinking and creation. In this way, the project also reflects a central cultural value of Tuvaluan society: "Kaitasi" - the principle of always shaping one's own life in connection with the community. An idea that could hardly be more relevant in our time.

d'une rive a l'autre is a work of daunting complexity. In a "live" staging, drums and metal discs are center stage; a series of 16 sound curtains of plastic and metal with exciter resonators activated by foot pedals surround the stage. All the musicians sing and speak traditional Tuvaluan songs and poems as well as singing freely adapted poems drawn from multiple languages. It comes as both a CD and a DVD. The CD was recorded over four days in the Südwestrundfunk Baden-Baden studio. It has 17 tracks and represents something like the totality of the audio work. The DVD was recorded with an audience in the Tollhaus Karlsruhe a day later. It has 12 tracks, is significantly shorter, sacrifices the instrumental duets, but is enriched by sheer theatrical intensity. Either way, it's stellar work, with Niggenkemper's insistence on a humane art reflecting both human potential and the necessity of engaging our collective condition with work of special power. The multiple demands that he places on his musicians are answered with stunning results in the additional tracks on the studio recordings, reflecting the brief individual duets among the matched instruments.

The DVD performance was also presented on the Free Jazz Blog at the time of its release, and it remains available online. It's an immediate introduction to the work's combination of visceral emotional power and often luminous instrumental textures:

https://www.freejazzblog.org/2025/03/pascal-niggenkempers-tuvalu-ensemble.html

Marta Warelis's Still Life with Lemons (Relative Pitch) may be less immediately shaped by environmental concerns than the preceding, but lyric ideas of landscape and the impress of environment still figure in her compositions, from "Birds" to "The Sky Blushes Sunset" to "Ashes to Sea." The group is a multi-national sextet, with the Polish pianist/synthesist Warelis joined by Hollander Ab Baars, clarinet, tenor saxophone; Canadian Karen Ng, clarinet, alto saxophone; Norwegian Ingebrigt Håker Flaten, double bass; and Americans Ben LaMar Gay, trumpet and electronics and Frank Rosaly drums and gongs. That might suggest a forceful, wind-driven ensemble, but the emphasis is reflective, intimate, sometimes pensive, often witty. Thin instrumental textures predominate, sometimes with different instruments' sounds penetrating one another, even creating beat patterns as pitches approach one another.

The opening "Birds" begins with an extended solo piano passage immediately emphasizing a certain intimacy. It will persist as the horns enter, with significant dissonance, in a slow interweaving of instrumental voices, ultimately matching the longing of the winds' theme against the chaotic rush of Warelis and the rhythm section. "There to the Bridge," an Albanian folk song, receives a plaintively nostalgic performance with Gay setting the mood before the two clarinetists carry the mournful theme to its furthest reaches. The band possesses genuine wit, as apparent in "Alternate Endings," continuously propelled by Warelis and Håker Flaten's broken rhythms, effectively extended by the flaring tone of Gay's trumpet and the dense squawking supplied by Baars' tenor saxophone. "Intermittent Web of Sorts" proceeds from the initially hesitant patterns of Håker Flaten and Rosaly before Warelis and Gay introduce the theme, textures gradually accumulating. It ultimately reaches an accumulation of sustained winds and electronics, pitches sliding in and out of beat patterns, a high point in the music's special interconnectedness.

(c) 2026 Stuart Broomer
items._cn_summary: 本篇乐评聚焦于三张2024年秋季录制的自由即兴与作曲交融的实验音乐专辑，涉及Magda Mayas领衔的八重奏Filamental、Pascal Niggenkemper的Ensemble Tuvalu以及Marta Warelis的作品。Mayas的《Murmur》以钢琴、两把竖琴、两把大提琴、双簧管与单簧管及小提琴的罕见编制展开近38分钟的自由即兴，灵感源自椋鸟群飞（murmuration）的集体协调意象，声响呈现为细腻的颗粒化与偶然性事件。Niggenkemper与Warelis的作品则在作曲与即兴的比重上各有侧重。整体音乐定位于当代实验即兴与室内乐交汇地带，由小众独立厂牌Relative Pitch等发行，展现了欧洲前沿即兴音乐对集体演奏形式与自然隐喻的深入探索。

items._cn_summary: Palagoma 是肯尼亚实验组合 ODD OKODDO 与资深肯尼亚歌手 Ogoya Nengo 的合作专辑。ODD OKODDO 以将传统卢雅族音乐与前卫声响解构相结合而闻名，本作在此基础上进一步深化，邀请拥有深厚传统根基的女声 Ogoya Nengo 参与，形成传统人声与实验乐器之间的张力对话。专辑延续并超越了其前作 Negore 的方向，体现出从即兴摇滚向更广阔声景探索的演进。作为东非地区的跨文化合作项目，专辑融合了非洲传统音乐元素与实验前卫手法，在保留本土文化身份的同时探索当代声音的可能性，具有鲜明的地域特色和艺术实验性。

items.body: Is it possible to protect a family member from the horrors of war? This question was posed in the film “Life Is Beautiful,” which inspired Ukrainian artist Halyna Andrusenko to create her own works of art, which in turn inspired the documentary by Joel Espi and the score by Daniela Mars, and whose title is shared by the opening track. Since the early days of the invasion, Ukrainians have been wrapping monuments and statues in cloth and reinforcing them with sandbags to protect them from fire and bombs. In her art, Andrusenko does the same with her family (allowing them to breathe of course) and draws sketches of them: a brand of performance art translated to physical form. Through flute and wordless voice, Mars conveys feelings of love and protection, with a melancholy undercurrent that highlights the fragility of human life. “Life Is Beautiful” is short yet sweet, a choral preface to the overture. Mars’ multitracked voice becomes that of a church choir, blurring the lines between baptism and requiem. Threaded into the following piece, the voice becomes the accompaniment for an array of flutes, operating as an additional instrument. Even without seeing the film, one can imagine the tenderness shown by Andrusenko as she wraps her family fold by fold, and the mixed feelings as she ties the cloth in string. “Colours of the Bending River” operates in the lower register, a cluster of dark thoughts. “Dana Nobis Pacem” (“Give Us Peace”) cements the spiritual connection. Part of the Latin Mass, the phrase also appears in works by Beethoven and Vaughn Williams. This prayer leads to the first of three versions of “Halyna’s Theme,” which is also the first of two contrabass pieces that represent the album’s emotional center. The contrabass take on “Dark Sky Lullaby” conjures images of its title; in Ukraine, these skies are as often caused by war as by weather. “In the Sky” is the score’s most abstract piece, a shimmer of dismay including a disturbing rustle at 00:50. Light and dark continue to battle, Mars’ voice a perennial reminder of hope. The later tracks grow more intimate with the sound of breath. “Halyna’s Theme (by the water)” offers early confidence, communicated by multiple flutes, before one steps to the fore, is heard and is then joined again, a parable of community. “Dark Sky” is balanced by “Silent Light,” the title a sideways allusion to “Silent Night.” We don’t know how the film ends, because we don’t know how or if the invasion ends. We do know that the war will leave a residue of sorrow. Mars conveys this beautifully in “The Wind Breathes,” leaving us with the bittersweet feeling of a mother who does what she can, knowing that it can never be enough. (Richard Allen) If you are in Kyiv, be sure to check out the exhibition, which just opened at the Dymchuk Gallery run by Max aka Trinidad Shevron!
items._cn_summary: 这是乌克兰艺术家Daniela Mars为纪录片《Protected》创作的原声专辑，以长笛、无词人声与低音提琴为核心乐器。音乐呈现当代古典与氛围音乐的融合，带有明显的暗色调与精神性元素——多重叠录的人声模拟教堂唱诗班，营造出从洗礼到安魂的仪式感。专辑灵感源于乌克兰艺术家Andrusenko用布料包裹家人以保护他们的行为艺术，以及俄乌战争背景下对古迹的防护实践。音乐传递出温柔、忧郁与人类脆弱性的复杂情感，低音提琴段落构成情感核心，'Dark Sky Lullaby'等曲目具有暗氛围质感。整体呈现出电影配乐特有的叙事性，融合东欧文化语境与当代古典技法，在用户偏好的当代古典、暗潮氛围与世界音乐维度上有所交集。

items.body: Originally published in Melody Maker on May 11, 1996, Mark Roland’s review of Meat Beat Manifesto’s Subliminal Sandwich captured the arrival of a record that would go on to become one of electronic music’s most influential and genre-defining releases; republished here with permission, 30 years on. A feast of beats and all manner of exotic electronica Forget all those “Now That’s What I Trip Hop” compilations. Forget also all the half-arsed post-modern samplist outfits who regurgitate large chunks of old soundtrack albums, couch it in cod theatrical mystique and are thought of as weird by people who play the album at dinner parties. Meat Beat Manifesto are back. Jack Dangers has spent the last several years plunging into what could have been a one-way expedition into the history of sound. Before he made the step from post-rave dance progenitor, author of blueprints taken up with gusto by the likes of The Prodigy, The Future Sound Of London and Transglobal Underground, to pith-helmeted explorer lost in the jungle forever, Jack Dangers has managed to deliver this massive missive. Spread across two CDs (for a limited time, anyhow), Subliminal Sandwich is a feast of beats and all manner of exotic electronica. A one-way expedition into the history of sound :: On first listening there’s an apparent schism between the two CDs. The first is recognisable as your standard format; songs, some singing here and there, all in all not a radical departure from 1993’s Satyricon. Cut-ups from old toasting records have produced two of its most thrilling tracks; “Nuclear Bomb,” an irresistible rhythmic assault of dub bass, lush textures and the ranting toaster, and “Assassinator.” The monstrous “Cancer” a melancholy and bleak excursion, is another spine-shuddering high point. The second CD is a non-linear monster of an achievement. Apparently, the whole thing was put together using some super synth from the Seventies, the sort of gear used to generate sonic blurts for analysis on an oscilloscope. It’s not one long gasbag of sub-Orb pointless noodling though the machine has been coaxed into jumping through all manner of hoops. “Mad Bomber/The Woods” provides an eminently suitable future soundtrack from the inevitable TV movie about The Unabomber while, as the rest of the CD gathers pace, gradually building into an almost painterly swipe of colours and textures. It arrives at Ketamine-induced nirvana with “Stereophrenic and “Simulacra” and understated, barely contained frenzy with “Electric People” This record won’t be scorching into the Top 10, but all your favourite household names will be first in the queue to buy it. You really should be joining them. Illustration, Design – Rich BorgeManagement [For Fastback Management] – Cathy CohnMastered By – Brian GardnerPhotography By [Additional] – Jay Blakesburg, Todd Della BellaProducer, Engineer – Jack DangersVoice, Bass, Waterphone, Bass Clarinet, Mellotron, Theremin, Synthesizer, Samples, Turntables, Other [Dishes] – Jack DangersWritten-By – Jack Dangers (tracks: 1-1 to 1-7, 1-9 to 2-10), Keith Dobson (tracks: 1-8) Subliminal Sandwich is available on Play It Again Sam, Nothing, and Interscope Records.   Meat Beat Manifesto · Subliminal Sandwich (Extended Version)
items._cn_summary: Meat Beat Manifesto 1996年双碟专辑《Subliminal Sandwich》是电子音乐史上极具影响力的作品，横跨断拍、工业电子、氛围声响与Dub等多种风格。第一碟延续此前结构化路线，包含融合旧唱片切片、Dub低音与人声采样的节拍化曲目；第二碟则以七十年代复古合成器构建非线性声响景观，被形容为色彩与质感的绘画式铺陈，呈现迷幻、实验性极强的声音探索。Jack Dangers 此前作为后锐舞时代电子先驱影响了Prodigy、Future Sound of London等艺人，此作进一步将工业电子与IDM推向更前卫的实验领域。该文章为1996年《Melody Maker》旧评的转载回顾，非原创评论。

items.body:
Good Morning Tapes back with a new album of lushest New Age sound-bathing x emotionally gooey trip hop from Andro Gogibedashvili aka Saphileaum, delivered in a mode that’s highly tipped for anyone on the line from Enigma to All Saints, from a.s.o to Boards of Canada.

Saphileaum has spent the past decade in passage between notable houses of atmospheric sorcery - Mule Musiq, Not Not Fun, Slow Life, Constellation Tatsu - and of course Good Morning Tapes, who now host their 3rd meeting, ‘Heavenly Hills’. A definitive chapter in his ten year saga, it is flush with symphonic strings and sky born keys, breezily urged by percussion that straddles chill out and folk zones. That said there’s also a Balearic - or should that be Black Sea? - appeal to its title tune, that lingers in the glistening wake of ‘Your Grace’, to the shimmering breaks of a parting piece ‘Alarko (Cosmic Eagle)’, falling into the space between Boards of Canada's cult-inspired hauntological nostalgia and Shackleton's hallowed ethno-dub.

“The tracks in the album were written with the inspiration of the kingdom of Shambhala in the Himalayas. I'm deeply fascinated and touched by it. Even the album title, holds the idea of its Heavenly nature and the tracks are like individual, elemental parts of it. The album is not a journey into Shambhala, but rather a play and a dance with its energy, image and presence in my world. Alarko (Cosmic Eagle) is dedicated to my grandfather, Temur Tsiklauri, and I dedicate the whole album to my country Georgia, which I deeply love.”
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是格鲁吉亚音乐人Saphileaum在独立厂牌Good Morning Tapes发行的作品，融合新世纪氛围、trip hop节拍与高加索地区的音乐色彩。以香巴拉为灵感来源，编曲包含交响化弦乐、漂浮键盘与融合民谣律动的打击乐层，在Boards of Canada式的怀旧氛围与Shackleton式的民族电子之间取得平衡。整体定位偏向氛围电子与世界音乐的跨界地带，兼具冥想感与节奏律动。独立厂牌背景与艺术家自身的格鲁吉亚文化视角为其增添了独特的地理与精神维度，人声与弦乐的铺陈营造出浓厚的精神性聆听体验。

items.body:
Munich drummer Captain Yossarian does Fela Kuti & Tony Allen worship with lean, dubwise panache and motorik regulation for limber groovers, emulating the adroit mixing desk chops of Dennis Bovell or Mad Professor’s discomixes in duration and loose durability.

"Please understand this work as a hommage to both musical cultures. The four tracks were chosen because they are a timeless witness to the political potential of music, that being proofed by their actuality. The songs feature essential dub eﬀects like echoes, reverb and filtering but also feature analogue sound eﬀects underlining and sonically illustrating the missing lyrical content. These vary from thundery spring reverbs and percussion instruments imitating the pouring rain on "Water No Get Enemy" to marching soldiers and shot gun like reverbs on "Zombie". From a cash register on "Expensive Shit" to the dub sirens created live on a Korg MS10 on "Everything Scatter".

Only analogue instruments, sounds and dub eﬀects were used on this recording. Mixing, dubs and arrangements were done live in consecutive sessions. The premaster was done by Sodi Marciszewer at Zarma Studios (Fela Kuti, Femi Kuti, Seun Kuti, Damian Marley) on the original Decca desk used by Fela Kuti in Lagos. Fela Kuti In Dub was conceived and produced by Cpt. Yossarian alias Manuel da Coll musician, producer and soundman from Munich/Germany. His last work "Bob Marley In Dub" (2021, Echobeach) attained a lot of critical acclaim and was featured by Don Letts on BBC6, the Riddim Magazine and Helmut Phillips book "DUB - The Sound Of Surprise" amongst others."
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由慕尼黑鼓手Captain Yossarian（Manuel da Coll）制作，将Fela Kuti与Tony Allen的Afrobeat经典作品以dub手法重新诠释。制作仅使用模拟乐器与效果器，混音与dub处理在连续现场会话中完成，最终在Fela Kuti当年在拉各斯使用的原版Decca调音台上完成母带处理。选曲涵盖"Water No Get Enemy"、"Zombie"、"Expensive Shit"和"Everything Scatter"等具有政治意味的曲目，融入了弹簧混响模拟雷雨、军鼓声效模拟行军脚步、现金机音效以及Korg MS10现场制作的dub警笛等丰富的声音设计。这是世界音乐与电子dub制作的一次跨文化融合，保留了原作的政治张力，同时以模拟质感赋予新的聆听维度。属于独立制作体量下的致敬型实验项目，在dub工艺与非洲音乐传统之间建立了有意义的对话。

items.body:
If Devon Rexi did Memphis-meets-chaabi-and-singeli, it may sound like Nicolini’s latest for their shared label South of North, melding fanciful, Arabic-style autotune and fizzing offbeats with trunk-rattle 808s in rudest, loosey-goosey style.

‘Quita Maldicion’ is Nicola Reverda’s 6th solo release on the label since his 2021 debut, over which time both artist and label have become go-to’s for weirdo, outernational-flavoured bops. The album’s 11 succinct vignettes tile up to a type of crazy-paving space between styles, Magpieing aspects of Memphis rap and Mahraganat dance-pop with a dub-wise, post-punk license and cheeky funk that works a treat, just like his chops with Devon Rexi - arguably one of the hottest live bands on road right now, especially with John T. Gast on the mixing desk. 

It’s not hard to hear Nicolini’s input on Devon Rexi surface across the album, from its spicy sirens and animated idents to the deftness of his wrong-footing grooves. It’s all there in centrepiece ‘Bottle J’, where steppas bass collides hip-shot sampler stabs and autotune, and likewise in ‘Girma Come In My Light’, but zipped up on a deep south rap downstroke. He’s also prone to hybridise gothic rap bells with grimy soca drums on ‘Rompe Mi Cabeza’, and fuse singeli with flamenco on ‘BBY Spoon’, or go like haywire digickal steppas on ‘Deep Tissue Killa Riddim’, all primed to send a dance hectic.
items._cn_summary: Nicolini的第六张个人专辑《Quita Maldicion》由小型独立厂牌South of North发行，是一张极度跨类型融合的实验性作品。音乐将孟菲斯说唱与埃及Mahraganat流行、桑给巴尔Singeli、弗拉门戈、索卡舞曲以及dub风格后朋克杂糅一体，配合阿拉伯式Auto-Tune人声处理和失真808低音。整张专辑由11首短篇组成，呈现出碎片化、拼贴式的结构，节拍在多种全球舞曲传统之间自由切换，既有俱乐部冲击力也带有解构意味。制作上与Devon Rexi乐队有深度交叉，John T. Gast参与混音。整体定位介于地下俱乐部实验与世界音乐融合之间，偏向前卫跳舞音乐方向。

items.body:
Donato Dozzy and Neel's critically lauded 2012 opus is re-pressed for 2026, highlighting just how influential it's been in the years since,

If you're into psychedelic, trance-inducing minimal techno, then you've probably come across Voices from the Lake already. If not, then prepare yerself for an interface with yr new favorite album. Released over a decade ago, the record made an immediate connection with clubgoers searching for a lysergic alternative to minimal's booming, avoidant monotony. Dozzy and Neel approach their tracks with enviable restraint: kick drums are present on the self-titled album, but forced into submission, not dominating the tracks but occasionally adding punctuation to their whirling structures. The key to each segment - which run into each other to form a longform heat haze of abstract percussion and offworld sound effects - isn't the drums exactly, but the mood the two Italian veterans are able to extract using only the most spartan ingredients.

The elements are familiar - cycling melodic phrases, distant pads, unstable rhythms - but the way Dozzy and Neel assemble them feels human and connected. On 'Iyo' there's barely a chance for the track to develop into a proper banger; all tension, no release. Elsewhere on 'Manuvex' the kick is softened into a damp thud, left to underpin shivery Porter Ricks-esque glitches and peculiar, dissonant synthetic elements that breathe with rare humanity. With the shortest track weighing in at a generous seven and a half minutes, and the longest hitting 16, it's an epic that's not afraid of simmering in its own juices until it's fully cooked. Bit of a classic?
items._cn_summary: 意大利双人组Donato Dozzy与Neel于2012年发行的迷幻极简techno专辑，2026年再版。该作以极度克制的制作手法构建长时间跨度（7.5至16分钟）的电子声响空间，底鼓不再主导节奏而是作为间歇性标点存在，配合循环旋律短语、远距氛围铺底、不稳定节律及外太空音效，形成抽象打击乐与氛围纹理交织的热浪式结构。评论指出作品以最简原料提取出罕见的情绪温度与人性化连接感，在极简techno的框架内拓展了迷幻与氛围的边界，被视为该领域的经典之作。整体定位为地下电子场景中具有持续影响力的标杆专辑。

items.body:
Surf Gang co-founder Harrison follows his work on MIKE and Earl Sweatshirt's 'POMPEII // UTILITY' with his first solo album, a tight set of wonky, atmospheric instrumentals that establishes him as one of rap's most reliable minimalists.

Harrison's been around for ages - he even held the camera on those Spooky Black videos back in the day - but it was only this year when his profile really spiked. Previously an almost anonymous presence alongside Evilgiane in New York City's Surf Gang collective, Harrison's work on 'POMPEII // UTILITY', an ambitious double album that he produced almost single handedly, took his name far beyond Reddit threads and YouTube credits. And the modestly titled 'Taking a walk & calling a car home' arrives only a matter of weeks later, sweeping up 10 of the beatmaker's oddest cues, collaborations with Bryce Byrd, Cajm, Earl Sweatshirt, Elipropperr, Harto Falión and TAKA and moody solo experiments that help establish his lore. On the opener, for example, the expected roll of clipped hi-hats and booming 808s never arrives; instead we're trapped in an uncanny back alley, met with saturated FM pads, ghostly moans and pulsing bass twangs.

Alba Collective's ambient/improv operative Byrd shows with an assist on 'graffititowers1&2', a squashed, Actress-like house sketch with breathy Y2K synths and London's Cajm, who we last spotted working alongside Bianca Scout, appears on 'Fieldsloop', a glitchy rumble of clicks 'n cuts percussion and booming bass. Even when Earl joins for 'officeloop with t + e', the mood never ruptures, carrying Surf Gang's most ambient ambitions into unknown territory with ratcheting foley clanks and reverberating woodwind loops. And when Virginia rapper Harto Falión breaks the silence on 'Wrong', it's with wordless chants that sound more horizontal than Harrison's comparatively upbeat kicks and snaps. It's worth holding out until the title track, six minutes of submerged, almost dubbed-out rhythms, Badalamenti keys and cryptic SFX that helps us contextualize the entire record. Whatever Harrison's doing, it's not strictly rap, that's for sure.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是纽约制作人Harrison的首张个人器乐作品，延续其与Surf Gang及Earl Sweatshirt合作中的极简制作美学。十首曲目融合了环境电子、故障节拍、dub式律动与氛围音景，FM合成器音色饱和幽暗，foley采样与木管循环构建出诡异的空间感，乐曲虽源于嘻哈制作语境，但实际更接近实验电子与暗潮氛围的交界。合作者中Earl Sweatshirt的说唱并未破坏整体氛围走向，Harto Falión的无词吟唱亦呈水平化处理。标题曲以六分钟的潜没式节奏与Badalamenti式键盘收束，奠定全作的暗色基调。整体定位介于地下嘻哈制作与实验声响探索之间，对电子/氛围/故障音乐爱好者有较高契合度。

items.body:
Dead strong etheric elisions of chamber-jazz, trip hop and dream-pop from Bristol’s Tara Clerkin Trio, following up their acclaimed self-titled debut with a new EP of subdued but glowing reveries somewhere between Dominique Lawalrée's intimate parlour music, Third Eye Foundation's atmospheric configurations and the sort of skewed pop we'll always associate with the Laika x Moonshake axis. 

The effortless drift of ’In Spring’ is the trio’s 2nd vinyl release after 2019’s eponymous debut and a tape with Dublin’s Weeding in 2020. It’s a distinctly Bristolian affair in its beatdown pacing and smoky atmosphere, which the label themselves compare to the roster orbiting the city’s Planet Records (Flying Saucer Attack, The Third Eye Foundation) in the ‘90s, with hints of a less noirish Portishead, or the sweeter ends of the Young Echo sound.

'Memory' dissolves into the atmosphere, all muted woodwind and organ moans that erupt into a half-time drum warble; if trip-hop is back in 2021, "In Spring" recalls the genre's most low-key and thus enduring moments, while harmonizing with the wyrd-world narco-pop abstraction of contemporary forces Cucina Povera and Leila Sakini. 

Their elegant chamber sashay ‘Done Before’ carries Tara’s vocals on beautifully buoyant string and piano phrases trimmed with a sort of tripped sensibility, and ‘Night Steps’ pushes that aspect with crushed drums and filtered vox that feel like Teresa Winter on a Portishead track, and their nuanced range finally reaches into a sort of modal, 4th world lounge style recalling Julia Holter via Air on the impessively accomplished title tune. 

A quietly brilliant, memorable record >> Tipped!
items._cn_summary: 布里斯托Tara Clerkin Trio的第二张黑胶作品，融合室内爵士、trip-hop与梦幻流行元素，呈现出烟雾缭绕的慢速律动与氛围感。专辑以木管乐器、簧风琴、弦乐与钢琴为底色，搭配碎拍与人声处理，风格介于Dominique Lawalrée的沙龙音乐与Third Eye Foundation的氛围电子之间，兼具Laika/Moonshake的偏斜流行质感。作品涉及'第四世界' lounge风格，与Cucina Povera、Leila Sakini等当代抽象流行力量产生共鸣。整体属于低调而精致的跨类型融合，在实验电子、自由爵士与世界音乐交汇地带找到了自己的位置，厂牌将其与Flying Saucer Attack、Portishead及Young Echo声景相提并论，体现了布里斯托独立音乐场景的独特脉络。

items.body:
London’s Joe Milli makes it two outta two with a 2nd Livity Sound session wriggling in the space between UKF, outernational offbeats and hard groove techno.

The dancer’s joy of pure repetition fuels Milli’s follow-up to the ace ‘Deep Forest’ 12” of 2025. Four-to-the-‘floor kicks knit with potent polyrhythms and Brazilian hoots and hollers in the brisk, sinuous hard groove of ‘Retreat’, and ‘Mantra’ keeps the pace up there with coiled subs and acres of space between the drums for proper loosey goosey movers. On the other hand, ‘Revival’ yokes it back to a heavier, syncopated sort of proto-UKF hoof, adjacent gqom and UK Afro-house flavours, and ‘The less You Know’ also pares it back to slinkiest triplets for clockwork hips.
items._cn_summary: Joe Milli是来自伦敦的电子音乐制作人，这是他在地下厂牌Livity Sound发行的第二张EP，延续了其音乐路线。整张作品在UK funky、硬核groove techno与世界音乐元素之间寻找平衡。四首曲目各具侧重：'Retreat'以四拍底鼓编织多重复节奏，融入巴西传统人声与喊叫采样；'Mantra'保持高速推进，蜿蜒的低频贝斯线与大留白鼓组形成张力；'Revival'转向更厚重的UKF律动，靠近gqom与英国Afro-house风格；'The Less You Know'则回归简约三连音，强调舞者髋部律动。整体定位偏向俱乐部舞池场景，节奏设计复杂且注重身体性，融合了多地域音乐元素，是一张兼具律动感与跨文化质感的地下电子作品。

items.body:
Alex Nut ushers his new band of crackshot players, Sum Of Its Parts, on a pair of lush jazz and beatdown cuts, backed with Boddhi Satva remixes.

Opening out into deep, jazzy space limned on his ‘Under Construction’ EP in ’25, Alex Nut gathers Sum Of Its Parts, aka Sam Crowe (Lianne La Havas) on keys, Junior Ali-Balogun (Sault/Cleo Sol) on percussion and Duane Atherley (Kokoroko) on bass, to explore expensive jazz horizons in the 8 mins of woozy sway to ‘The Message’, while locking tighter into a Detroit beatdown house shuffle ‘Hello High’ surely winking at classic KDJ and Theo Parrish. Brussels’ BBE & Yoruba regular Boddhi Satva resets ‘The Message’ to a sort of slowed, dubbed, and triplet-metered broken beat hustle in his signature Ancestral Soul style, and farther swept out with a dusky appeal on its dub.
items._cn_summary: 这张EP由Alex Nut主导，汇聚了多位英国当代爵士圈的乐手，包括来自Kokoroko、Sault及Lianne La Havas团队的成员。原创曲目横跨深沉爵士即兴与底特律beatdown house两种风格，编曲松弛而层次丰富，明显受到Theo Parrish和KDJ等前辈的影响。布鲁塞尔音乐人Boddhi Satva的混音版本则将作品引向非洲祖灵回响（Ancestral Soul）与碎拍领域，融入放慢与三连音节奏处理，带有明显的非洲散居文化色彩。整体定位为爵士、电子舞曲与世界音乐之间的跨界融合，制作精良但实验性有限，适合喜欢爵士与电子交汇地带作品的听众。

items.body:
Surface Access chases a pair of ace dub techno 12”s for Nico Jaar's Other People with two more strips of claggy depth for East Paris label 59 Bel, tipped FFO Sa Pa, Intertoto, vintage Chain Reaction.

Both sides fathom flooded catacombs of club music for anyone bored with modern techno excess and seeking more muted immersion in the dance. In that sense, A-side ’Status.Density’ brings heads deep inside his sound with careful unfolding of FX envelopes drawing bodies into echoic play of shivered, coruscating chords and skudgy bass for nearly 10 minutes, and acting as entry portal to the more reserved depths of ‘Immersion Thrust’, packing more info in the low end shifts and yoked-back, smeared textures that plunge like the most mesmerising Substance & Vainqueur works.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张由East Paris小厂牌59 Bel发行的Dub Techno 12英寸作品，与Nico Jaar旗下的Other People厂牌有关联。音乐风格深入Dub Techno与Club Ambient的交界地带，融合了回响深沉的Dub质感、Techno节奏骨架与实验性的声响设计。整张作品以绵密的低频、层叠的效果器包络和模糊失真的和弦纹理为核心，营造出类似地下空间的沉浸式声场。A面以约十分钟的渐进式展开作为入口，B面则更趋内敛，以低频位移和粘稠的质感纹理向纵深推进。整体定位面向厌倦主流Techno冗余、追求深度沉浸感的电子乐听众，声音处理精细且具有较强的个人美学。

Out of earshot for a minute, Voices From the Lake regroup around familiar aquatic themes on the satisfyingly immersive ‘II’. Signature Italian sound sensitivity and attention to spatialized detail meets subtle rhythmic urges for an hour of slowed, aquaplaning groove and crystal clear tone
items.body:
Donato Dozzy & Neel’s beloved ambient techno project return with a 2nd raft of floating, swaying structures some 13 years since the their maiden push-off, reliably reprising the formula of their expansive epic.

Out of earshot for a minute, Voices From the Lake regroup around familiar aquatic themes on the satisfyingly immersive ‘II’. Signature Italian sound sensitivity and attention to spatialized detail meets subtle rhythmic urges for an hour of slowed, aquaplaning groove and crystal clear tones that dive off from deep ends of ‘80s new age ambient, and its ‘90s techno descendants, into an elemental sound world idealised for horizontal listening - or perhaps a slinky eyes-shut bop, if the mood takes.

It’s all too easy to slip into anodyne flotation tank waft within this realm, but the finely attuned sensitivities of Dozzy & Neel buoy this one, like their previous, to a point of usefulness as meditation aid and ambient music that harmonises with the background of whatever space it’s projected into. Blessed with restraint yet richly resonating across the frequency spectrum, the 10 tracks flows naturally from the stealthily unfolding envelopes of ‘Eos’ thru properly charming offbeat pulses in ‘Ian’ that surely evoke a sort of underwater xmas vibe in the same way we hold AFX’s SAW 85-92 as a seasonal perennial.

““The project was never meant to become what it did,” the duo reflect. “At one point, we even paused it. Only to later embrace it in all its forms. II is both a continuation and a reinvention.” True to that spirit, Voices From The Lake have explored extremes in recent years, from high-tempo live sets to seated listening concerts, while remaining anchored in the meditative pulse of ambient techno. II extends this lineage, carrying forward the immersive sound design and boundary-pushing vision that has defined their work from the beginning.”
items._cn_summary: 意大利双人组Voices From The Lake时隔十三年推出的第二张专辑，延续了其标志性的氛围 techno 路线。作品以水生意象为线索，将八十年代新世纪氛围音乐的空间感与九十年代 techno 的节奏脉搏相融合，营造出适合平躺聆听或闭眼律动的沉浸式声场。Donato Dozzy与Neel以意大利声音美学中对空间细节的敏感著称，专辑十首曲目在克制与丰富之间取得平衡，从极简铺陈的Eos到带有离拍律动的Ian，音色清澈透明，低频深沉。整体延续了既有的公式化框架，在氛围 techno 范畴内属于精致成熟之作，但并未在声音设计或结构上展现出突破性的实验意图。

items.body:
Parasymbiosis – the ability of two separate organisms to exist closely together

"I have long pondered the concept of connectedness in relation to life’s existence. The Dalai Lama teaches that destruction of one’s neighbour equates to destruction of oneself. In contrast, modern Western culture has placed the individual at the epicentre of existence – to the detriment of non-humans and humans alike. Ecological Memory influences present or future responses of a community; it is this shared memory that enables organisms, objects and the environment to connect to each other, and to the other. What happens when a community or ecological system loses this memory, this connection? The systems begin to break down; intergenerational memory evolves in rapid short steps, culture and connection becomes unrecognisable. Time speeds up.

Yet with the naked eye, the universe reflects slow time. Its very distance provides a sense of stasis. Understanding the night sky could very well be the vastness of time we have forgotten through our ecological memory, our loss of the visible difference between the likes of night and day; non-referenceable and dictated by intangible rhythms that exist beyond the cyclic elements of nature.

Through Parasymbiosis I imagined sounds of the inherent connection between the earth and the universe. Contemporary society has rendered invisible the heritage of the night sky and what it teaches us. The wonder and awe it inspires, in its pure, unadulterated form untouched by light pollution and modern satellite activity, has always informed non-human and human life cycles and human culture. In modern times, only 40% of human beings can still see the Milky Way. We have forgotten that the dark sky and the earth reflect each other – they are, as a metaphor, parasymbiotic.The Electric Cristal (EC) features strongly in Parasymbiosis. It is a microtonal, electro-acoustic instrument that has captured my imagination through its deep and fragile resonance created by touching glass rods encased in aluminium. Ceated by Dylan Crismani (AUS) in 2019, the EC conjures vast soundscapes. Electronics exploit the volatile vibrations and random frequencies that the instrument generates."

items.body:
A note from Callum Mintzis

"Folds of water sanctify the river. Tracing soft, cool hands, the tall oak make way for a child who is older now. The moon gives chase, as clouds attempt to climb her. And choiceless, she falls through, further out of sight. An episodic, dreamlike place; Headwater is an invitation to explore what is fundamental to life – as if asking the listener; what, after losing my compass, is the nature of my experience?

The headwater is the childhood of the stream – its beginning. And as though banished from the safety, innocence and purity of this place, the individual is carried through rapids, gashed and sawn, calling for the self to be woven again. In these early moments, the poignancy of this venture is felt in droves – a woman lost in the forest trying to find a way out, silhouette skating through light while something approaches, further out of sight.

Everyone is thrown out of childhood – hurled into a life to make sense of something which lives on in memory. The mind catches fragments, painted by ink found in the canals of the veins and rivers within – their headwater, the heart. Like tentacles beneath our skin, their message arrives unannounced, while a great struggle embarks to keep them at bay – the clarity of their awareness polluted.

After a time, the river is older now. The forest’s foliage has tuned, sculpted and moulded her – so much so, that the water is barely recognisable. But the girl is no fool, and her sensitivity will not be auctioned. Catching glimpses of the headwater – she cries out to the forest and the valley. This time, unafraid of the pain it wears and hides behind, pretending.

She sings to the eclipse, crying for the stars and their breath on the river’s back. Calling for the animals, insects and fish - bowing to the scent of the pine in the evening warmth of the air, weeping to the memory of her childhood, she comes alive. Only in such a surrender does the headwater of her tears make itself known, and all that is longed for arise without having ever been lost.

Could she really be creating all of it? And like a child with a boundless imagination, be confusing her role in the play with the candid, honest face of life itself? Humility might yet speak – claiming all she has taken herself to be as the leaves and foliage which pollute and fragment the stream. That a quest to return to childhood is an unnecessary one – because the currents which begun at the headwater still contain, at every step of the river, the headwater itself. And that the cries and memories heard starkly through the forest valley have still come from the deepest waterways the body has pronounced.

And so, originate in the heart – and are no threat."

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由Helen Svoboda创作，发行于澳大利亚实验厂牌Room 40，定位为现代古典与氛围音乐的交汇地带。乐评以极为文学化、诗意的笔触展开，通篇以河流、森林、童年、记忆等意象构筑隐喻，将专辑描绘为一段关于失去与回归的声音旅程。Room 40厂牌长期深耕实验氛围领域，相关推荐包括Akio Suzuki、Lawrence English等知名声响艺术家，显示出该厂牌在探索性聆听体验上的稳定品质。音乐风格上偏向冥想式氛围文本与新古典质感的结合，适合沉浸式聆听。评论本身缺乏对具体声响设计、编曲手法或结构安排的直接分析，但厂牌背景与分类已足以将其归入与用户偏好高度契合的氛围/当代古典范畴。

items.body:
Kosmiche krautrock mainstay Harald Grosskopf operates at full wingspan on a new raft of astral-planing arps and motorik pulses laced with wistful extended melodies and atmospheric sleaze, together with a titular nod to Miles Davis’hinting at the album’s underlying theme: the productive friction between man and machine.

"For the uninitiated, Grosskopf’s career spans six decades of German music history. From early beat groups in Hildesheim, through Krautrock propulsion with Wallenstein, cosmic explorations alongside Ashra, and defining work with Klaus Schulze, he has consistently pushed rhythm into evolving technological contexts. His 1980 solo debut Synthesist, previously reissued on Bureau B, helped establish a sequencer-driven language that bridged kosmische tradition and modern electronic form.

Created over three to four months in his garden studio, Glitches Brew is shaped by speed and responsiveness. Grosskopf worked primarily with digital instruments this time, travelling light and favouring fast access from feeling to recording. Ideas arrive spontaneously; he works until satisfied, often reshaping sounds the next day if they fail to spark with the same intensity. What emerges is a vivid, present-tense record where human instinct and electronic process remain in constant, audible conversation. Stems are recorded in mono or stereo, passed through a Studer desk and printed to two-track, restoring weight and tactility to digital sources. Where VST synthesis can lack transient bite, analogue circuitry restores what he calls the sensation of leather, wood and metal. The signal path is humanised without surrendering to nostalgia.

The opening track, “Leisure Life,” establishes the album’s language immediately: low-end bubbles and chewy filters pulse beneath crystalline sequencers and shuffling hats. Optimistic pads bloom around frazzled lead lines as the piece glides forward, building toward a rolling bass climax that feels both euphoric and grounded. Grosskopf has long embraced the click track, relishing the freedom it brought during sessions for Klaus Schulze’s Moondawn: when rhythm is sequenced, the drummer is freed from marking the “one,” and can instead explore texture and propulsion. That commitment to free movement persists here.

On “Spheroids,” stargazing synth motifs orbit percolating bass and alien percussion, slipping into a techno-pop wormhole. Midway through, dramatic trills rupture the flow like a gravitational tear before the groove reasserts itself with cosmic poise. “Flow” descends into colder terrain: icy chimes shimmer above a slow, low rhythm, while snaking lead lines and robotic churn carve through gloomy pads, creating a hypnotic, glacial drift.

“Stranger Strings” pushes further into the uncanny. Warped electronic strings emerge from cavernous reverb and short delays, entangled with mechanical pulses, whirring and hissing as if half-forgotten machines were stirring back to life. Yet Grosskopf never lingers in abstraction for its own sake. “Panta Rhei” snaps the album back into direct physicality, a driving, rhythmic surge pierced by heartrending synth strings and blinking circuitry, all anchored by the mother of all mutant funk basslines. It is elastic, restless and gloriously corporeal, a blast of body music which reaffirms his belief in groove as emotional catalyst.

“LiLaLu” shifts the mood again. Sampler voices and Fairlight-era textures drift through a shimmering digital dream, conjuring a romantic escape on the shores of the Sea of Tranquility. It’s space-age spa-core in the lineage of the old Innovative Communications aesthetic - retro-futurist, tender and quietly playful. By contrast, “Kalter Lärm” closes the album in uplift: rave-style hits, expansive pads and a roving bassline gather collective momentum, shoulders rolling and arms aloft, before dissolving into cosmic bliss.

Grosskopf has spoken of the early thrill he felt hearing The Beatles, the breathtaking shock of newness, and of the early 70s Berlin scene’s determination to detach from Anglo-American models and pursue something wholly original. That refusal to look backwards still guides him. Synthesisers were never retro fetish objects but tools of liberation, instruments capable of breaking from guitar history and opening fresh terrain, and he continues to embrace whatever technologies expand the field of possibility.

Glitches Brew balances analogue intuition and digital immediacy, kosmische heritage and contemporary electronic language. It is the work of an artist still following his own ideas, still excited by sound, still testing the edges. Sixty years on from his first beat-group rehearsals, Harald Grosskopf remains what he has always been: a musician for whom rhythm is liberation, technology is possibility, and the future is something to invent again and again. – Patrick Ryder, 2026"
items._cn_summary: 德国电子音乐先驱Harald Grosskopf的最新专辑，将Krautrock的motorik节奏传统与Kosmische太空感延续至当代电子语境。Grosskopf跨越六十年德国音乐史，曾与Ashra、Klaus Schulze合作，1980年首张个人专辑《Synthesist》确立了序列器驱动的电子语言。本作以数字乐器为主干，模拟电路润色信号路径，探讨人机之间的摩擦与对话。曲目涵盖'Leisure Life'中低频气泡与水晶般序列器的交织、'Spheroids'的星际合成器主题与techno-pop隧道、'Stranger Strings'中扭曲电子弦乐与机械脉冲的诡异融合。整体定位介于Kosmische传统与当代电子舞曲之间，节奏感强烈，声响设计兼具数字锐利与模拟温度，是德国电子传统的延续与再创造。

items.body:
Much needed reissue of Stephen Hitchell’s sleepwalking dub house trips, faithfully remastered by Pole for posterity and optimal immersion. FFO Maurizio, GAS, Shinichi Atobe.

Echospace’s Stephen Hitchell is in his element as Intrusion on two durational treks deep into the studio haze. Also found in much longer versions on original release, back in 2015, ‘A Gentle Embrace’ appears here thru13 min timeframes ideal for long blends in-the-mix, or more simply enjoyed on their own, floating and soporific terms.

The original puffs up a sublime architecture of diffused fumes and rolling, velvet-coated bass that yearns upward, outwards with a gorgeous sense of deferred gratification that he tempers to an even more light-headed feel in the B-side reduction, whisking the choral pads and chords to cirrus wisps and beatific harmony.
items._cn_summary: Stephen Hitchell以Intrusion名义发行的dub house长篇作品再版，由德国电子音乐人Pole操刀重新母带处理。音乐呈现出深沉而迷幻的氛围感，以弥漫的烟雾质感和天鹅绒般厚重的低频为基础，辅以合唱式pad与和弦铺陈，营造出催眠般的漂浮听感。整体风格介于minimal dub techno与ambient之间，与Maurizio、GAS、Shinichi Atobe等艺术家的美学谱系一脉相承。作品以十三分钟左右的时长结构展开，适合长时间混音或独立沉浸聆听，体现出Echospace厂牌标志性的空间纵深与冥想气质。

items.body:
Natty digi-dub frolics from Mermaid, a Japanese reggae dub and chamber music fiend, doubling down on his ’25 debut LP with 10 takes on Bach, Gossec, and trad Japanese songs inna dub style FFO Tapes, 7FO, Froid Dub, SKRS Intl., Disrupt.

One up to their debut LP, ‘Dubmaid’, Mermaid’s 2nd set pairs ostensibly, mutually exclusive bedfellows under the same sheets on handfuls of bubblers defined by piquant melodies and ruggedest, sine wave-sculpted bass. The combo works a treat for those who like to dance between styles, across borders, registering big cuts in his ludicrous flip of ‘Air on a G String’, and a nice ’n easy version of Gossec’s C.18th work ‘Gavotte in D’, and a Japanese traditional ‘1st January’ named ‘New Year’ and strapped with bubbling bass, also teased out in wilder dub on ‘Long Ago’. DJs and dancers also need to test out the moon boot cosmic skank of ‘A Nap’, and the Tempo Riddim-riffing ‘Lucifer’.
items._cn_summary: 日本制作人Mermaid的第二张专辑《DUB FOREVER》，延续首作《Dubmaid》的路线，将巴赫、戈塞克等西方古典室内乐作品与日本传统民谣以数字dub手法重新演绎，共收录十首改编曲目。旋律线条灵动，配以正弦波雕刻的低频质感，曲目涵盖《G弦上的咏叹调》的dub化翻转、戈塞克十八世纪《G大调加沃特舞曲》的悠闲改编，以及日本传统新年民谣的多版本bass化处理。这是一张跨越古典室内乐、东方传统与电子dub的跨界作品，在西方古典、日本民俗与reggae/dub之间寻找独特交汇点，整体偏向小众独立场景，体现出明确的实验意识与个人美学，但dub美学本身并非纯粹的前卫实验范畴，定位介于世界音乐、电子制作与古典重构之间。

items.body:
Hessle/Timedance alum Bruce steps up to remix the entirety of Bristol-based post-rock outfit Quade's tender, Talk Talk-indebted second album, infusing its folk-inspired songs with space, distortion and serious bass weight.

When Quade were working on their first album, 2023's 'Nacre', they tapped Larry "Bruce" McCarthy, an experienced engineer as well as a notorious beatmaker, to handle the mix. So when they finished their even more convincing follow-up last year, they handed him the stems, trusting him to take the tracks wherever he saw fit. His full suite of versions compliments 'The Foel Tower' well; we were already sold by the cinematic original and McCarthy reduces each track to its component parts, adding subtle effects and enhancing the general ambiance. 

The best example might be 'Bylaw 7.1', a track that already felt like a tribute to Graham Sutton's work with Bark Psychosis. McCarthy extends the 3:49 original to almost six minutes, waiting until the final third to even drop a bass note. After the chilly, electric piano-led intro, the brushed drums hit like a brick to the face, peppered with tape-fucked vocal echoes and fluttered drones. And he takes a similarly destructive approach to 'Canada Geese', shredding its dreamy textures and driving it towards a noisy, psychedelic crescendo that's positively nightmare inducing.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是电子音乐人Bruce对Bristol后摇滚乐队Quade第二张专辑的完整再混音作品。Quade原专辑受Talk Talk影响，带有民谣元素和电影感氛围；Bruce拥有Hessle Audio和Timedance等实验电子厂牌的制作背景，将原曲拆解重组，融入失真效果、低频重量、磁带处理和无人机式音墙。代表曲目如"Bylaw 7.1"将三分多钟的原作扩展至近六分钟，前段以电钢琴冷峻引入，后段刷鼓与失真人声突袭；"Canada Geese"则将梦幻织体撕裂，推向噪音与迷幻的高潮。整体呈现后摇滚、氛围电子与实验声响的跨界融合，兼具情绪层次与声响探索。

items.body:
Balmat alum Patricia Wolf flits to Ransom Note’s ambient tape series with a 45 min session of carefully pruned synth wooze and new age whims evoking private press cassettes via early ‘90s garden centres.

"‘Yarrow’ is a bouquet of new music by Portland, Oregon-based musician and field recordist Patricia Wolf, marking the label’s ninth release and the third of Season Two. The works are her reflections on the life cycle of plants and their dynamic ecological relationships.

Wolf created the album in response to her artist residency at the Rocky Mountain Biological Laboratory in Gothic, Colorado, as part of the Art-Science Exchange Project in the summer of 2024. She worked closely with ecologists Dr Paul CaraDonna, Dr Amy Iler, Dr Jane Ogilvie, Dr Nickolas Waser, Dr Mary Price, and Dr Will Petry, spending weeks engaged in long-term research on plants, pollinators, and their interactions as the climate changes. 

Each track on Yarrow looks at a different part of a plant’s life. The songs touch on the conditions that plants need to grow, the quiet life of roots, how flowers attract pollinators, and the strength of seeds. The first single, 'Inflorescence', the scientific name for the floral display that a plant makes in an effort to reproduce, captures this event in song. The music slowly builds layers, reflecting the album’s overall feel. The album ends with the majestic Boards of Canada-esque 'Adapted for Extreme Conditions', and the entire b-side features Patricia’s field recordings from around Gothic, Colorado, and a guided meditation by Dr Paul CaraDonna, whose research inspired the project, inviting listeners to tune into the sounds and activities of the ecosystem."
items._cn_summary: 帕特里夏·沃尔夫是来自美国波特兰的田野录音师与电子音乐人，本专辑为她在科罗拉多落基山生物实验室艺术驻留期间创作的系列作品，以植物生命周期与生态关系为核心主题。音乐以合成器氛围铺陈为基底，融合田野录音与新世纪元素，整体气质趋向冥想与自然主义。作品按植物不同生长阶段组织结构，配器上具有九十年代私人磁带出版物的怀旧质感，尾声带有低音质慢速电子风格，B面收录大量环境声学录音与一段由生态学家录制的冥想引导。专辑体现了将科学田野观察转化为声音艺术的跨学科实验思路，由独立小厂牌以磁带形式发行，是融合氛围、田野录音与生态主题的小众电子/实验类作品。

items.body:
One of the weirdest gadges in UK dub flexes his authority on unique concoctions of roots reggae, digidub, cumbia, and folksy chamber drone for the Breadminster Board of Abstinence. big tipped FFO Nearly God, Tapes Lee “Scratch” Perry & The Congos, Elysia Crampton, DINTE archives.

In cool pursuit of his reggae-voiced folk covers LP for FatCat, ‘Perpetual Musk’ - and 12”s for Accidental Meetings, Elijah Minnelli keeps it ideally offbeat with a deft, hands-on concision and deeply rooted steez throughout ‘Clams As A Main Meal.’ There’s a charmingly daft backstory involving oysters, frisky fictional villagers, and burnt-out hippies, that gives the LP its title, but let’s focus on the music here. 

It’s dead special stuff, surely certified by Dennis Bovell chiming in like all members of The Congos at once in the swaying harmonies knit to nyabinghi drums in ‘Canaan Land' somehow sounding like a score to an Emir Kusturica film, while Welsh singer Carwyn Ellis helps characterise Minnelli’s dare-to-differ audness on the sea-legged cumbia shanty ‘Donna Donna (Chwerthin)’ which clearly suits their lilt of their mother tongue. 

Elsewhere the producer’s feted dub tekkerz and feel for proper folk wise dub groove really come into play, in step from the jaw harp twang and jaw bone friction dematerialised in ‘Sumptuous Promise,’ thru a heavy lamenting ‘Watercraft Apologist’ that wouldn’t sound out of place in a Mark Jenkin flick, to the insectoid digidub of ‘Calopify Now!,’ gently psychoactive cumbia of ‘Bomb the Green Belt,’ and ghostly chamber keen of ‘Long Conifer.’ Play it over and again!
items._cn_summary: 英国制作人Elijah Minnelli在《Clams As A Main Meal》中将根源雷鬼、数码dub、昆比亚与民谣室内drone融为一体，形成跨类型的声音实验。Dennis Bovell参与的曲目展现出nyabinghi鼓与dub制作的深厚功底，威尔士语昆比亚民谣《Donna Donna (Chwerthin)》融入地方文化色彩。专辑同时包含口簧琴声响的解构、迷幻昆比亚与幽灵般的室内低鸣，呈现手工质感与前卫意识的结合。小型独立厂牌发行，延续英国地下dub传统的实验脉络，与实验电子、世界音乐及当代室内乐均有交集。

items.body:
Maiden vinyl reissue of legendary Arabic grooves and spicy electronic organ sauce from a bygone Damascus, helmed by Assa’d Khoury’s psyched Farfisa keys and rife with killer, hand-played percussion. 2nd hand copies are nigh-on impossible to find! A delectable knees-up FFO Omar Khorshid, Islam Chipsy, DJ Niraha.

“Long a highly coveted find for DJs and vinyl collectors worldwide, Assa’d Khoury’s 1978 album Electronic Touches Belly Dance has earned its cult status as one of the most sought-after instrumental LPs from the region. This release marks the very first reissue of the album, which has remained virtually impossible to find since its original pressing. Khoury (1953–2020), a Syrian virtuoso pianist, violinist, and leader of the "Spring Band," bridged Levantine tradition with the cosmic, psychedelic textures of the late 1970s. As Dikraphone's Ahmed Khalil notes in his introduction, the music serves as "a sensory portal to a bygone Damascus, where a psychedelic Farfisa and mesmerizing rhythms create a unique groove" that remains remarkably fresh today.

The album’s history is tied to the legacy of the venerable Lebanese Chahine family. Mozart Chahine, son of the inventor of the quarter-tone keyboard, founded the Byblos label to champion music from the region. In an exclusive interview conducted by Mario Choueiry (IMA), he recalls encountering Khoury at his Damascus music store and recording the entire album in a single day. "The musicians were seasoned, much like jazzmen," Chahine reminisces, noting that the session captured a rare, immediate energy between the ensemble members.

The musical journey spans the Arab world, offering electronic reinterpretations of Arabic standards and paying respect to Egyptian master Sayed Darwish. From Mohammad Abdel Wahab’s "Ahwak"—rendered here in an almost psychedelic version—to the Lebanese traditions of Melhem Barakat, the record culminates in the avant-garde "Al Ghaba." An original Khoury composition with a killer groove, "Al Ghaba" is a very funky highlight that has become particularly popular among Arabic music crate diggers. Closing the album in style, it perfectly fulfills Khoury's intent: a sound for modern times, reaching toward a futuristic energy that remains as potent now as it was in 1978. A cult classic which Wewantsounds is delighted to reissue and which will surely please all Arabic groove lovers."
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是叙利亚音乐家Assa'd Khoury于1978年录制的阿拉伯器乐作品的首次黑胶再版。音乐以迷幻法尔费萨电子风琴为核心音色，融合黎凡特传统手击打击乐，将阿拉伯经典曲目以电子化、迷幻化的方式重新演绎。专辑横跨阿拉伯世界音乐传统，涵盖从埃及大师赛义德·达维什到黎巴嫩梅莱姆·巴拉卡特的作品，原创前卫曲目"Al Ghaba"以强烈的放克律动成为掘金乐迷的热门。整体呈现出七十年代末的宇宙感与未来主义气息，将中东传统旋律与电子声响进行了富有实验意味的结合。由独立再版厂牌Wewantsounds发行，作为长期被DJ和收藏家追捧的cult经典，展现了非主流音乐地区独特的文化视角与跨类型融合价值。

items.body:
A Note from Aviva

"Following our 2024 self-titled release, Nick and I were compelled to make another record, expanding on the distinctive sound world we have found as the duo Driftwood.

Grounded in the unique instrumentation of two microtonally re-tuned pump organs, alongside clarinets and guitars, the sonic landscape of Driftwood has become a welcoming place for us to inhabit together. The distinctive characteristics of these instruments, as well as the challenge of playing multiple instruments simultaneously, have become a frame we've leaned into more and more, trusting the vitality of their combined resonance to lead us further into uncharted paths of improvisation.

For our second album, we wanted to incorporate additional elements from each of our solo practices into our sound: modular synth, effects pedals, electric guitar and contact mic’s (because playing two instruments at the same time wasn’t enough for us!) In ‘Maps’, electronics are subtly worked back into the original improvisations, saturating the live instrumentation with bass undertones and signal processing, pushing the sound into more otherworldly realms. Sometimes the pieces hint toward song-like forms, with repetitive guitar ostinatos lulling the music to the edge of familiarity, while other times the drones and harmonies blur, creating the ground from which glimpses of folk-like melodies surface, as if from a long-forgotten dream."
items._cn_summary: Driftwood是双人组合Aviva与Nick的实验即兴项目，专辑《Maps》以两台微音律重调的簧风琴为核心乐器，辅以单簧管、原声与电吉他，并融入模块合成器、效果器与接触式麦克风。作品以即兴为框架，将原声乐器与电子信号处理相融合，嗡鸣式和声与零星的民谣旋律片段交替浮现，音响呈现出远离常规的异世质感。整体定位介于当代自由即兴、实验电子与新民谣之间，强调乐器自身共振特性与同步多声部演奏的技术挑战，编曲思路具有较强的探索性与个人化色彩。

Second outing for German artist Arovane and American artist Taylor Deupree via LAAPS.

"Aquainted through their shared love of music technology, and now a friendship, this is the second-time pairing between German artist Arovane and American artist Taylor Deupree after their first release together in November 2022: 'Skal_Ghost' on 12k.

This new release explores once more an organic journey built around loops and layers or processed and re-processed sounds giving this particular color to a must-have album."
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是德国电子音乐人Arovane与美国声音艺术家Taylor Deupree的第二次合作，通过独立厂牌LAAPS发行。两位艺术家因对音乐技术的共同热爱而结识，此前曾在12k厂牌合作发行过作品。音乐风格延续了两人的实验电子路线，以循环与层层叠加的处理声音为核心，构建出一种有机流动的声场质感。声音经过反复处理与再处理，形成独特的色彩层次。整体定位于氛围电子与IDM之间的实验地带，偏向冥想式的聆听体验。Arovane以精细的碎节拍和微观声响设计见长，Deupree则擅长极简氛围织体的营造，两者的合作在技术与美学上都有较高契合度。适合偏好电子、氛围、实验声响的深度听众。

items.body: Air Signs rests at its distinct sound. Everything is pieced together very well, and all the noises, melodies, and synths are family—they all align track after track. Deschamps has a gift for cohesion. Even when he’s working with degraded loops, reversed recordings, and heavily processed guitar, nothing feels fragmented. Everything belongs. Dreamlike and reminiscent of ambient joy Air Signs by anthéne   Brad Deschamps has been quietly building one of the most consistent catalogs in contemporary ambient music. Working under the anthéne moniker, the Toronto-based musician has released extensively on Home Normal, Past Inside the Present, Whitelabrecs, and Constellation Tatsu, while also running the widely respected Polar Seas Recordings label. His collaborations with Ian Hawgood (as Rosales), Stijn Hüwels, and David Cordero have earned critical acclaim, and his solo work is known for its dusty, emotionally resonant guitar and synth-led compositions. Air Signs arrives on Dronarivm, a small independent label from the Netherlands focused on contemporary ambient, electroacoustic, and modern classical music. Each piece here feels very dreamlike and reminiscent of ambient joy. A very easy listen. Inspired by a hawk that landed right outside the window at Deschamps‘ workplace in a hectic area of downtown Toronto, the pieces are light and airy, reflecting the stillness of our natural surroundings in the midst of human-made chaos. Dronarivm has built a strong catalog over the years, releasing work from artists like Chihei Hatakeyama, bvdub, and o[rlawren], all mastered with care and presented in limited physical editions. “Starling” and “all a blur” are standouts here. “Starling” has such a beautiful build to it with subtle guitar noises. Deschamps processes his guitar loops with a Chase Bliss Lossy pedal and a Vongon Paragraphs filter, both creating unusual tones, overtones, and artifacts. He also makes heavy use of a Maneco 16 second delay for lo-fi forward and reversed loops. This approach to guitar processing is what sets Deschamps apart from more straightforward ambient guitarists—the loops are degraded, filtered, and stretched until they’re barely recognizable as guitar. Rather than letting the track fade out into nothing or meaninglessness, “Starling” adds meaning through a steady bassline that anchors the swells and melodies drifting above it. Creating haunting, otherworldly textures (in reverse) :: “All a blur” is where Deschamps uses backward recordings and noises for reversed melodies. Writing reversed melodies is a craft that’s both detailed and tricky. When you reverse a recording, the attack and decay of each note flip—what was a sharp pluck becomes a slow swell, and what was a fade becomes an abrupt cut. This means that composing in reverse requires you to think backward about how sounds will evolve. It’s not just playing something and hitting reverse; it’s imagining how the reversed version will sound and then recording the forward version in a way that creates the desired effect when flipped. Sometimes it works beautifully, creating haunting, otherworldly textures. Sometimes it doesn’t, the timing feels off, the melody doesn’t resolve the way you’d hoped, or the reversed artifacts distract from the composition. Deschamps fits this perfectly here. At its core, “all a blur” sounds nightmarish, but it really isn’t. The reversed elements create an unsettling undercurrent, but the piece never collapses into darkness. It’s tense without being oppressive. Air Signs rests at its distinct sound. Everything is pieced together very well, and all the noises, melodies, and synths are family—they all align track after track. Deschamps has a gift for cohesion. Even when he’s working with degraded loops, reversed recordings, and heavily processed guitar, nothing feels fragmented. Everything belongs. The mastering by Peter Andersson helps too, giving the release a warm, unified sheen that ties the six tracks together. Air Signs is limited to 100 copies on factory-pressed CD, packaged in a unique discbox slider case with a soft-touch finish. For fans of guitar-based ambient and electroacoustic music, this is a strong addition to both Deschamps‘ catalog and Dronarivm‘s growing discography. Air Signs is available on Dronarivm. [Bandcamp] Air Signs by anthéne
items._cn_summary: 这是一张以环境音乐为核心的专辑，由多伦多音乐人Brad Deschamps以anthéne之名创作，发行于荷兰独立厂牌Dronarivm。作品以吉他循环和合成器为主导，但通过Chase Bliss Lossy效果器、Vongon Paragraphs滤波器以及Maneco延时等设备对音源进行深度处理，呈现出颗粒感、失真和拉伸的非常规音色。专辑中的反向录音技法尤为突出——作曲时需逆向思考音符的起音与衰减演变。整体氛围轻盈梦幻，带有lo-fi质感与声响实验性。专辑以多伦多市中心一只降落的鹰为灵感，尝试在人造喧嚣中捕捉自然的静谧时刻。作品在环境音乐框架内融入了电声实验与声响设计手法，属于独立小厂牌范畴的扎实之作。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — Behind the title paraphernalia of The Great Parrot-Ox and The Golden Egg of Empathy, the third studio album from The Claypool Lennon Delirium project lies a conceptual work that carefully addresses the oversimplification of human life by a certain use of Artificial Intelligence, which would result in a simplification of the universe in the form of clips. Metaphors aside, the album finds them more intertwined than ever... Lennon's psychedelia combined with Claypool's funk rock, meeting once again in a story that reveals them as more progressive than ever.It encloses all the acid of Gong's synthesizers in a 60s psychedelic pop and then you get WAP (What a Predicament), like a firefly trapped in a glass jar...Les' bass is taken to another context, even more so with the mellotron in the background, or the choirs, and it is there where this union is most successful from a compositional point of view, because from an instrumental point of view their interaction was also proven.There are sitars on The Wake Up Call, and the spacey spirit is identified as the project's DNA. Lennon's keyboards are more prominent than on previous releases, adding another layer of depth to the desired direction. Meat Machines begins with a chorus followed by a guitar reminiscent of Genesis, while the bass sounds different, no longer like Primus, but with a different color that subtly contributes to the overall sound, without lacking personality. There are classic Moog solos, followed by the guitar in a very Bach-like ending.Troll Bait, on the other hand, advances with powerful bass and organ hits like 70s Hawkwind, with an almost operatic spoken-word vocal part carried out by Les Claypool, a strong percussion progresses while the theme becomes darker...and suddenly a very clean guitar solo emerges above the surface, this is definitely a different album.Simplest of Deeds deepens the psychedelic journey...as we delve into Heart of Chrome, where electronica contributes to this dreamy atmosphere in what is revealed as the heart of this conceptual work, reminiscent of both Eloy in the past and the Australians King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard. Through the Horizon follows and is my favorite track on the album, where the synthesizers and bass kick in, with Les singing almost lyrically, while the Zeppelin-esque drums advance slowly, without haste...and the bass at the service of the symphonic keyboard...until it decides to hurry and those classic choirs rise along with it, while the guitar stops accompanying and does a solo until Mantra of the Manatee takes us back to that London of the 60s carried by the guitar and bass at the same time, between chorus and chorus with luminous keyboard, until it turns funky.The Golden Egg of Empathy features a prominent bass with a mellotron in the background, sounding like Stanley Clarke!, plus the prophetic choir driving the story forward, creating a very strange atmosphere...until Cliptopia takes up this dark psychedelia again, this time more rock-oriented, with Parliament-Funkadelic-style choirs, disguising itself as "Bootsy" Collins for the occasion.Once again, percussion, bass, keyboards, and electronic elements create a festively strange atmosphere in Cliptron Scuttle, before Melody of Entropy begins to close the curtain with that twilight aura of Pink Floyd, led vocally by Sean Lennon and creating epic atmospheres until the grand finale of It's a Wrap, a psychedelic-pop suite where at times they recall Stereolab, the first part with Sean, and the second with Les, in an album that sounds challenging, modern, and with the best of the classicism of the past, all with a homogeneity that makes it their best work to date, one where two become one.
items._cn_summary: 这是Les Claypool与Sean Lennon合作项目的第三张录音室专辑，以迷幻摇滚与放克摇滚为底色，融合六十年代迷幻流行、前卫摇滚与电子声响元素。专辑以概念化方式探讨人工智能对人类生活简化这一当代议题，编制中运用Mellotron、Moog合成器、西塔琴等乐器，呈现出Gong、Genesis、Hawkwind等经典前卫乐队的影子。贝斯演奏作为核心驱动力，与键盘和吉他形成丰富对话，作品在迷幻空间感与放克律动之间游走，兼有复古音色与现代主题意识。整体定位为折衷前卫摇滚，注重多元素融合与叙事性概念构建，独立厂牌发行。

items.body: Review by sgtpepper — It's great that the band release a live album in this line-up incarnation. Essential pieces of the 73-74 era are included, one from the masterful debut album and even a packed jam "Asbury Park".There are many instrumental highlights but the interplay between the bass and drums is worth calling out. Bruford clearly enjoys a room for improvisation and Wetton's aggressive playing style complements the essential dynamic sound.I have the newer USA live version, which includes "Fractures" which I'm very happy to be included. The density, tension and guitar playing are magnificent, especially in the ominous end.To sum it up, the material and playing are excellent but one would hope for a better overall sound (even though the instruments are distinctive) and greater length ;)
items._cn_summary: King Crimson 1974年阵容的现场录音专辑，呈现了实验前卫摇滚的巅峰面貌。乐队成员包括吉他手Robert Fripp、鼓手Bill Bruford、贝斯手John Wetton和中提琴手David Cross，该阵容以高度即兴化和张力化的演奏著称。专辑收录了1973至1974年间的代表性作品，涵盖首张专辑中的经典曲目以及即兴段落较长的"Asbury Park"。评论特别强调了贝斯与鼓之间的器乐互动、Bruford在即兴中获得的自由空间以及Wetton激进的贝斯线条如何构成动态声响。整体音乐密度高、张力强，吉他演奏在阴沉的尾段中展现出强烈的表现力。该专辑体现了前卫摇滚与自由爵士即兴传统的深度融合，在器乐复杂性和声响探索方面具有显著的艺术价值。

items.body: The Witch Said No is a relatively obscure project from Russia that has been active for several years and has already released a number of recordings in its home country, including a debut album. Very little is known about the project itself, which only adds to its mysterious aura. Earlier this year, the band released a new EP through the Slovak label Aliens Production, featuring three new tracks alongside six remixes. The Witch Said No delivers a powerful form of Dark-Electro driven by bombastic heavy beats and overwhelming repetitive sequences, topped with an almost completely unintelligible, hateful vocal style. The title track is certainly an interesting discovery, while the two remaining new songs follow a similar direction but prove slightly less convincing. The remixes of the title track were created by KIFOTH, Deadjump, Human Vault, Novakill, and TC75. The EP also includes an alternative version of an older track. What stands out most here is undoubtedly the title track itself, which shows strong potential, alongside several successful remixes — especially Novakill’s contribution, which turns out to be my personal favorite. (Rating:7). Listen to “Call The Dead”: https://aliensproduction.bandcamp.com/track/call-the-dead
items._cn_summary: The Witch Said No 来自俄罗斯，是一支活跃多年的暗潮电子项目，在斯洛伐克小厂牌 Aliens Production 发行了数字 EP《Call The Dead》。音乐风格属于典型的 Dark-Electro，以沉重的鼓点、压迫感极强的重复序列和几近难以辨识的嘶吼式人声为特征，气质阴暗且具有侵略性。EP 包含三首新曲与六首混音，标题曲被认为最具潜力，Novakill 的混音版本是亮点之一，但其余新曲的说服力稍显不足。整体制作偏向该类型内部的常规表达，缺乏明显的跨界融合或声音设计层面的突破，但在暗潮/工业领域仍属扎实之作。

items.body: Damage Code Digital Slaves Miseria Records Damage Code is the new project from Carlos Grabstein and Ben Bunzen of 89s✝︎ and Hammershøi respectively, and deals in a very specific style of old school EBM. Forgoing the oft-taken route of Nitzer Ebb and DAF worship, the duo instead deal in a sound that recalls a swathe of body music acts from Europe that emerged in the early 90s (think Escalator and Aircrash Bureau) that took advantage of advancements in digital electronics while maintaining a healthy amount of grit in their design. As such, Digital Slaves is a record that doesn’t break much in the way of new ground, but makes an impact by keeping its tracks impactful and fast moving, usually running a single groove as hard as possible from beginning to end. Grabstein and Bunzen certainly know what they’re doing with that approach and it pays off well in plenty of the record’s nine tracks; “I’m Sick of These Pigs” has a rhythm that just keeps getting heavier as it progresses, the gravitational pull of its bassline and drums warping its sweeping noise, and monotone vocals towards it. Alternately, Notausgang collab “Monotonia” is all about how its gated pads and samples and echoing synthlines create syncopation, the bass tuned down to a low rattle. There’s a real charm to just how rough and ready Damage Code keep matters without repeating themselves too often. There’s a healthy dose of funk in the awkward tripping-over-its-own-feet synthline on “Menschen im Glitch” and the chintzy fm stabs of “Esclavo Digital”, but neither track cannibalizes the other’s appeal through repetition. A lot of it has to do with pretty canny if uncomplicated sound design choices, such as the wonky spring reverb and belt sander saturation of “Lessons in Pain” and the claustrophobic delays of “Berlin”, which sounds like it’s closing in on you if listened to on headphones. Old school body music is almost a genre that lives and dies by how it balances the appeal of its throwback approach without just recreating the same songs over and over again. It’s weird to think of such a straightforward genre having much in the way of subtlety, but on Digital Slaves Damage Code certainly make a case for how much you can squeeze out of it through strength of craft. Buy it. Digital Slave by DAMAGE CODE The post Damage Code, “Digital Slaves” appeared first on I Die: You Die.
items._cn_summary: Damage Code的《Digital Slaves》是一张扎根于九十年代初欧洲老派EBM（电子身体音乐）传统的专辑，回避了Nitzer Ebb和DAF的常见模仿路径，转而以Escalator和Aircrash Bureau等更冷门的身体音乐乐队为参照。专辑共九首曲目，以单一律动的强力驱动为核心策略，制作风格粗粝直接，鼓机与贝斯线制造出沉重压迫的节奏基底。单声道人声、门控合成器、低频颤动、弹簧混响和磁带饱和等声音设计选择体现出不复杂但有效的匠心。某些曲目融入放克元素和FM合成器戳奏，增添了变化感。整体而言，这是一张以扎实工艺取胜的复古取向EBM作品，未在类型框架内做出显著突破，但凭借制作水准和对律动张力的把控，在老派身体音乐的谱系中占据一个稳健的位置。

items.body: Alan Trench (Orchis, Temple Music ...) en Martyn Bates (Eyless in Gaza, Sorry For Laughing) zijn al sinds 2000 bezig met dit samenwerkingsverband en vonden sedert 2018 onderdak bij het eigenzinnige Italiaanse Final Muzik label. Sedert die tijd reviewen we hier ook bij Dark Entries de eigenzinnige, vaak conceptuele en andersoortige muziek van dit uitzonderlijk duo die beiden een verleden kennen in meer industriële en experimentele muziek. In Twelve Thousand Days trekt de band veel meer de kaart van de donkere, avant-garde folk, ietwat vergelijkbaar met wat je soms op albums van Current 93 hoort om een ietwat meer gekende naam in deze review te gooien, luister maar een keer naar “Asphodel Flowers”. Alle songs zijn als het ware op zichzelf staande verhalen die allen samen ook weer een groot verhaal vormen. Vol mysterie, een soortement ‘spleen’ (lichte depressie) maar dan wel eentje met oog voor natuur en schoonheid in de tristesse. Met deze “As The Moon Draws The Tide” is Twelve Thousand Days al aan zijn negende album toe, nu ja al, de groep is reeds actief sedert 2000 dus dat aantal valt in al die jaren enigszins mee. De sfeer van het album wortelt in de Britse traditie van mythologie en poëzie, het geluid is eerder minimalistisch en bij tijden zelfs breekbaar, met de ‘klagende’ stem van Martyn Bates in de hoofdrol. De akoestische gitaren worden ondersteund door sporadische percussie, orgel en her en der meer elektronische ambient aandoende soundscapes. Ze geven de nummers een wat bevreemdende, geheimzinnige sfeer die als het ware een soort natuurlijke adem is doorheen dit album dat ook door liefhebbers van pagan folk zal worden gesmaakt. Met Twelve Thousand Days komt als het ware de Britse folktraditie samen met de meer donkere post-industrialscene waar beide heren ook hun sporen in verdienden. Dit album, hoewel de zomer voor de deur staat, representeert eerder de korter wordende avonden en het verval dat in het herfstseizoen zijn magische intrede doet. Om dit album te kunnen appreciëren, dien je tijd te maken, en je ergens op een knusse plaats te installeren, koptelefoon op je hoofd en wegdromen. Op de digipak zijn tevens alle teksten afgedrukt waardoor je in de nummers kunt meeglijden zonder je suf te denken over wat er nu precies wordt gezegd / gezongen. Melancholie is altijd een beetje pijnlijk, dat is een beluistering van deze “As The Moon Draws The Tide” ook, maar zoals eerder gesteld, in tristesse baadt ook schoonheid, luister maar een keer naar songs als “Notes From A Ruined City” (zie clip), “Upon The Blasted Heat”, “ Ghosts” of “ Heathen Dog”. Twelve Thousand Days (Facebook)
items._cn_summary: Twelve Thousand Days是Alan Trench与Martyn Bates的长期合作项目，由意大利独立厂牌Final Muzik发行。专辑定位为暗黑前卫民谣，融合英国传统神话诗歌元素与后工业场景的实验声响。Martyn Bates的吟唱式人声居主导地位，原声吉他辅以零星打击乐、管风琴及电子氛围音景，营造出神秘、忧郁、近乎脆弱的听觉空间。整体气质与Current 93相近，兼具异教民谣的精神性与氛围电子的疏离感，是英国民谣传统与暗黑实验音乐交汇的代表作品，适合沉浸式聆听。

items.body:
A little over a month ago, New Delhi imprint Antariksh Records and prominent streetwear/sneaker retailers VegNonVeg joined forces to launch KISSA In-Store radio, livestreaming and archiving sets from the latter's Gurgaon store. With the aim of curating "broadcasts for the curious", the mix and radio series has featured the likes of Unnayanaa, Bombie, Farhan Rehman and flux vortex.

As part of its aim to document and archive the current alternative listening practices around sound and amplification present in the city of Delhi-NCR, and International Synthesiser Day, KISSA In-Store Radio brought together the synth communities that have been quietly growing in the capital city.

Shiv Ahuja aka Songs For A Tired City took charge of the 3-hour special, representing Synth Hang, an organically growing group of synthesiser enthusiasts which started as informal at-home gatherings but has since evolved to involve the who's who of the city's synth acts with multi-faceted interactive live events and even internationally prominent figures like Laurie Anderson paying a visit. Alongside an interview, Ahuja performed a set based around the iconic synth Buchla Easel, weaving ambient and leftfield sounds to showcase Synth Hang's penchant for the same.

Shaurya Sarin aka Imerohi has been building the live event series, Alt Baithak. While not exclusively dedicated to synthesisers, Alt Baithak also fully dedicates itself to the experimental, both in terms of sound and event flow, as it features workshops, immersive rituals and film screenings besides live sets. Imerohi builds a similar sense to his KISSA In-Store Radio set, morphine his guitar and triggering synth patterns that traverse ambient, post-rock and club music.

Lastly, Ahuja brings in Aditya Ghosh who, as Angia, builds modules for Eurorack synthesiser systems and performs music for them. Doing the same for his set, Angia offers a pacier performance where four-to-the-floor grooves are teeming with arpeggios and melodies teeming with textures that cut through.

Head here to stream more sets from KISSA In-Store Radio, and follow Antariksh Records to stay updated.
