items.body:
Legends In Their Own Lunchtime: An Exploration Of The Canterbury Scene Aymeric Leroy (Cuneiform; Silver Spring, Maryland)

1970(April 10th, 1970 - IBC Studios, London)

Negotiations were now underway between Sean Murphy and several labels including Deram, CBS and Harvest, the EMI sub-label that had distributed Volume Two in the UK and already had Kevin Ayers in its stable. "They are still not an attraction in the very top bracket, so it was a pleasant surprise to see major companies throwing in genuinely massive bids earlier this year when the group was looking for a recording deal," Richard Williams revealed. Ultimately, Soft Machine signed with CBS, but Third was self-financed, taken partly from studio sessions, but also from live recordings ("Facelift") and edits and loops of tapes made by Mike Ratledge and Hugh Hopper at the home of Bob Woolford, who had let them use his Brenell and Stellavox tape recorders. Such infringements of accepted professional practices were only possible because CBS, having acquired a finished album, were no longer in a position to force the band to comply with them.

The benefit for Soft Machine in terms of artistic freedom is easy to measure. But this has to be balanced against the fact that the production on Third is, to put it bluntly, an unmitigated disaster. IBC, at the time the studio of choice for such notorious perfectionists as The Who and the Bee Gees, are probably less to blame than the band themselves who, in spite of the issues with Volume Two, are again credited as sole producers. The sound suffers from almost constantly saturated low frequencies and extremely vague mediums, the drums are much too low in the mix, as if played behind a closed door; and the organ is deprived of much of its biting impact through overwhelming equalization. Unfortunately the 2007 remaster, while an improvement, fails to rectify this.

What is problematic is that, as well as making the album an uncomfortable listen, its sub-par production lessens the claim, widely held at the time of its release, that Third represented musical state-of-the-art. This claim was based on Soft Machine's ability, unparalleled among their contemporaries, to draw from and amalgamate an exceptionally wide range of influences. Starting out as a rock band, and then gradually moving towards jazz to invent a uniquely personal, and absolutely valid, British answer to American fusion, Soft Machine went even further, incorporating the influence of Stockhausen's avant-garde and Terry Riley's repetitive minimalism. Third's 'total' vision, encompassing the entire spectrum of known musical genres, placed Soft Machine at the forefront of musical "progress" in 1970. However, horizons have since expanded to such an extent, beyond the Western tradition in particular, that this concept of universality has aged considerably.

In his insightful review of Third for Actuel, Paul Alessandrini wrote of "music to really listen to, no longer aiming for a purely physical vibration, more interiorized. Soft Machine have re-thought their musical influences - Riley, Cecil Taylor, Coltrane - to really make them their own, abandoning their aesthetics of random explosion in favor of a much more thought-out approach." There are still occasional reminders of these sonic excesses that, as Alessandrini noted, had now largely disappeared from their music. Mike Ratledge's lengthy solo introduction to "Facelift" almost sounds like an electric exorcism, as if to rid Soft Machine of what still remains of that violence in order to reinvent their music in a more controlled manner, setting formal perfection as their new objective.

Considered as a whole, Hugh Hopper's piece represents the last remnant of Soft Machine's early days, when they still favored spirit over form - here found lacking in both sound quality and performance, with a few train wrecks along the way - and were intent on disregarding the accepted rules. "Facelift" includes free sections increasingly at odds with Ratledge's preoccupation with structure - and while as a keyboard player, he still embodies the band's more radical leanings, Ratledge's own compositions reveal a much less iconoclastic temperament. Hopper described his own approach at the time as "halfway between" that of Dean, "whose thing is really total improvisation, without any structure, and on the other extreme, [that of Ratledge] who's into entirely formalized musical forms.

"Moon in June" completes Robert Wyatt's donation to Soft Machine of the material originally intended for his first solo album in 1968. It is interesting to note that Wyatt does this at the exact point where Soft Machine had shed any remaining reference to pop in their live repertoire. Looking back, Wyatt was certainly justified in saying that his side of Third was "the last chance I had to use all the things we'd done without being a jazz band. I wanted to get twenty minutes of it down somewhere." And since his colleagues, reluctant to act as mere accompanists, had made no secret of their lack of interest in his songs, he recorded most of "Moon in June" on his own, repeating the modus operandi of the 1968-69 demo. Hugh Hopper and Mike Ratledge's participation is again limited to the organ solo halfway through (Hopper also plays a short melodic theme earlier in the piece). Elton Dean wasn't asked to contribute anything - Wyatt's unconvincing justification being that he "hadn't yet worked out how to work on [his] stuff with the added wind instruments."

As there was no mention of this breach of band discipline in the sleeve notes, only the most astute listeners noticed that the organ heard during the first ten minutes was a Hammond rather than Ratledge's signature Lowrey, that the playing clearly wasn't Ratledge's, and that most of the 'bass' parts were played on an electric piano. When the truth was finally revealed, Wyatt gave contradictory versions of what had happened - in one interview claiming that Ratledge and Hopper had "refused to play [on "Moon in June"] and I had to play it all myself," in another that he'd "almost had to force them to get them to play on it, which I thought was rather unfair as I'd done my best to get into the music they were writing." Probably the most objective and believable of Wyatt's rationales was that he was "terrified it'd be played wrong" if he didn't perform it all himself.

To approach "Moon in June" as a 'message' song would misrepresent Wyatt's more mundane intent, insofar as the phonetic qualities of the words often seem to matter more to him than their meaning. In other words, "Moon in June" is above all a musical composition, a suite of instrumental sections, some of which are adorned with melodies and lyrics, and others not. The singing accompanies the music rather than vice-versa. In this respect, outside of a possible rivalry with Elton Dean and Wyatt's inability to sing while drumming, there was no theoretical incompatibility between Soft Machine's move towards jazz and the continued presence of Wyatt's voice (even if limited to the Echoplexed scat singing of his solitary interludes during the band's concerts). Dispensing with vocals was the single most questionable move in Soft Machine's entire musical evolution, not to mention one whose commercial consequences cannot be underestimated. In different circumstances, Hugh Hopper would surely have joined Wyatt in lobbying for having at least some vocals, but in addition to his increasingly strained personal relationship with Wyatt, Hopper had at this point completely lost interest in non-instrumental music. "I find that using the human voice means asserting limitations to your music right from the start", he explained in 1972. "I am more interested in the sounds generated by instruments, or electronic devices, because the possibilities offered by songs are much more limited than when experimenting with sounds."

Even if there was no future for singing in Soft Machine, "Moon in June" at least offers evidence that Robert Wyatt, in a voice-free context, could still be more than "a session drummer for an interesting new species of jazz groups," as long as he contributed to the writing. When it came to extended pieces, he could stand comparison with Mike Ratledge, even though he lacked any comparable academic background. In addition to its constant melodic inspiration, "Moon in June" is very skillfully constructed (indeed, its instrumental architecture had remained intact since 1968), and confirms Wyatt's seemingly innate talent for making a coherent whole out of ill-assorted musical ideas.

(c) 2026 Aymeric Leroy

items._cn_summary: 本文摘自探讨坎特伯雷音乐场景的专著章节，聚焦于软机器乐队（Soft Machine）1970年发行的第三张专辑。该乐队从摇滚出发，逐步融入爵士融合元素，并大胆借鉴施托克豪森的先锋派手法与特里·赖利的重复极简主义，构建出一种横跨多种音乐流派的'总体'美学视野。评论指出专辑制作质量欠佳，低频饱和、混音失衡，但肯定其音乐理念在当时的前瞻性。坎特伯雷场景本身即英国实验摇滚与爵士融合的重要支脉，与学院爵士、前卫实验和先锋音乐传统紧密相连。由独立厂牌Cuneiform出版，体现了对地下音乐史的严肃学术梳理。

items.body: The soundtrack to a new film about the Denver heavy metal four-piece takes the listener deep into an exploration of outer – and inner – space Photo credit: Alessandro di Martino In 2024, Blood Incantation released Absolute Elsewhere. One of the strangest, most compelling and original albums in heavy music of the past decade, it connected with a wide variety of listeners – many within and, crucially, an equal number outside the metal underground.The album used cathartic, whirling death metal with cerebral, unexpected pastures (ambient music, analogue synth freakout, gloriously complex prog passages, vintage kosmische panache) and – as is always the case with Blood Incantation – some serious world building. As intimate with Popul Vuh and Tangerine Dream as Morbid Angel or Death, Absolute... The post What Lasts is Consciousness: All Gates Open – the Original Motion Picture Soundtrack by Blood Incantation appeared first on The Quietus.
items._cn_summary: Blood Incantation 是一支来自美国丹佛的四人乐队，以将死亡金属与氛围音乐、模拟合成器、前卫摇滚和宇宙音乐（Kosmische）相融合而著称。他们的音乐风格跨越多重边界，既继承了 Morbid Angel 和 Death 的极端金属传统，又深受 Tangerine Dream 和 Popul Vuh 等德国电子/氛围先驱的影响。这张原声带专辑配合同名纪录片发行，其上一张专辑《Absolute Elsewhere》被评价为近十年来重型音乐领域中最奇特、最具原创性的作品之一。乐队的创作强调严肃的世界观构建和声音探索，融合了宣泄性的死亡金属、复杂的器乐编排以及模拟合成器即兴段落。该乐队签约于 Century Media Records（索尼音乐旗下），在保持地下精神的同时具备一定的商业基础。

items.body: Review by andrea — "Sunlight" is the second album by Drift Lab, a jazz rock project based in Rome and led by Manuele Montesanti. It was self-released in 2026 with a completely renewed line-up featuring, along with founder member, composer and leader Manuele Montesanti (piano, synths), the new members Marco Pistone (bass), Guido Della Gatta (guitars) and Roberto Porta (drums) plus the guest Carlo Maria Micheli (sax). According to the official website, this is music "written with rigour but performed with freedom, where improvisation finds its home within intricate harmonic architectures". Drift Lab is an open, constantly evolving project, aiming to shape a sound that blends "jazz roots and contemporary imagery, instrumental virtuosity and electronic curiosity, composition and experimentation". The art cover tries to give a visual form to the musical content...Electronic sounds and a brief drum roll introduce the album's title track, "Sunlight". It's a bright piece, full of frenetic energy, ready to wake us up to face a new busy day. A kind of urban ride illuminated by the sunlight...The following "Yellow Fire" is a piece with a jagged rhythm but full of warmth and melodic flares that leads to "Bump" a jazz rock track full of nocturnal and disquieting atmospheres with excellent interweaving of guitar and keyboard that share the solo parts, supported by a never banal rhythm section..."A-M-M-I-M" somehow revisits and reinterprets a piece from the previous album ("M-I-M-M-A"). It's a relaxed track that at times invites you to dance the night away while "Serendip" is a slow, sensual piece featuring guest saxophonist Carlo Maria Micheli and a certain oriental exoticism. The title refers to the ancient name of the island of Ceylon..."Chaste Countrywoman" starts with the bass in the foreground that traces a funky rhythm, then the electric guitar outlines melodic paths that take the song in other directions... Next comes "Bleep" is a complex and fast piece where all the musicians showcase great technical skills and a notable interaction."bYpOLAR" begins with an old video-game atmosphere and continues with irrepressible freshness, alternating more relaxed moments with others where the pace becomes pressing and lively. Ten, the dreamy "Evolving" concludes the album. A beautiful official video was shot for this piece, completing the sonic universe the band has evoked with images of a disturbingly beautiful dystopian future...On the whole, an excellent fusion work!
items._cn_summary: Drift Lab是一支来自罗马的爵士摇滚融合项目，2026年自资发行第二张专辑《Sunlight》。作品以爵士为根基，融合电子声响与键盘合成器，编曲注重复杂和声架构与即兴空间，乐手交替担任主奏。曲目风格多样，标题曲充满都市能量，《Yellow Fire》节奏锐利，《Bleep》展现技术互动，《bYpOLAR》带有复古电子游戏氛围。《Serendip》邀请客座萨克斯手加入，融入东方异域元素，呼应锡兰古地名意象。整体定位介于学院爵士与当代融合之间，兼顾技术性与可听性。

items.body:
A second pressing of last year’s gorgeous fourth and final album from Old Saw, the American Primitive project of Tongue Depressor's Henry Birdsey, riffing on the classic Takoma paradigm with additional ferric washes and layered instrumental drones, huge recommendation if yr into Bruce Langhorne’s ‘The Hired Hand’ or classic work by Daniel Lanois, Laraaji, Pelt, Stars Of The Lid, State River Widening.

'The Wringing Cloth' is Birdsey’s fourth and final Old Saw outing, and ironically it’s also the one that has garnered most amount of critical and commercial success. Old Saw’s shimmering, drone-heavy soundscapes were recorded on 1/4" tape at various locations in New England over the last few years and are once again paired with evocative black and white imagery from photographer Dylan Hausthor, whose landscapes somehow perfectly capture the timeless, widescreen appeal of the music inside.

Birdsey's pedal, lap steel and resonator are at the core of each track, but the album also features Old Saw’s usual personnel; Harper Reed on nylon string guitar and banjo, Ira Dorset on fiddle and bowed strings, Ann Rowlis on reed organ and harmonium, Jim Cutler on telecaster, Addison Starkweather-Price on bass, and Peter Catchpole on metal objects and power hammer. That lap steel lends the music its stylistic anchor, taking us through decades of American folk before gently fraying at the edges. Birdsey's application of classical minimalism - the themes that surge through his work with Zach Rowden as Tongue Depressor - is still somehow present here, especially as the record pulls into its second side and the shimmering country-fied atmosphere is pierced with bell-like sounds, but the overall mood and flavour of the record is distinctly easy on the ear and timeless in its appeal.

As the label put it, “What has always been uncanny about this music is that it arrives in a state at once familiar and obscured, like a memory weighed down with sensory information but no identifying details to place it. The Wringing Cloth walks off further into that geographical dream without time or language, until it’s just a speck of light….”
items._cn_summary: Old Saw是美国原声吉他流派（American Primitive）的项目，由Henry Birdsey主导，也是Tongue Depressor的核心成员。这张最终专辑以四分之一英寸磁带在新英格兰多个地点录制，融合了滑棒吉他、踏板钢吉他、班卓琴、小提琴、管风琴等原声乐器，构成厚重的无人机音景。音乐将美国民间传统与古典极简主义结合，呈现出一种在熟悉与陌生之间的模糊状态，与Bruce Langhorne、Daniel Lanois、Laraaji、Pelt、Stars Of The Lid等艺术家的气质相通。整体风格偏向氛围化的原声实验，在民谣根基上叠加了延伸技法与极简主义结构，介于美国原始吉他、氛围音乐和实验民谣之间。

items.body:
Shinichi Atobe fiends will be in their element with Yuji Takenouchi aka Mr. YT’s iridescent techno-house perlers, his first new material in years and the latest in Short Span’s stream of chef’s kiss goodies.

With ‘Universo’ Short Span look beyond contemporary circles to a cult Japanese artist renowned for a string of EPs in the late ‘90s, and Ron Trent co-productions in the mid ’10s, and only scarcely heard since then on his label Element of Souls. The four-tracker effectively picks up where he left the dance years ago, ushering bodies to effortless flight in a mode that reminds of Shiichi Atobe via Shed and Microworld style Detroit elegance in ‘Acuario’, flexing his fruitiest jazz-fusion-house chops on the whirring swang of ‘Escorpio’. He simmers it down to a breezier flow led by puckered, G-funky trills on ‘Tauro’, and smartly defers gratification on ‘Piscis’, blooming lushest harmonic pads that eventually sync with syrupy deep house grooves for graceful end-of-night business.
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑收录了日本地下音乐人竹之内裕二（Mr. YT）暌违多年的新作，由小厂牌Short Span发行。整体风格介于底特律优雅techno与深层house之间，融合爵士放克元素，延续了九十年代末日本地下电子舞曲的传统。共四首作品，从流畅的techno-house律动到更为内敛的deep house质感，编曲注重氛围铺陈与和声层次。与Shinichi Atobe、Shed等音乐人风格相近，同时融入了G-funk式放克律动与爵士和声线条。定位为面向舞池的精致电子舞曲制作，发行于小众独立厂牌，属于日本地下电子场景的回归之作。

items.body:
Bristol’s quietly revelatory Tara Clerkin Trio usher a magnificent new 30 minute mini album of folk-jazz and classical-downbeat chamber music x dreampop with their return trip for London’s World of Echo, hugely tipped if yr into Laika, Pram, Broadcast, Hydroplane, A.R. Kane, Portishead, Laila Sakini.

Effortless and transcendent, Tara Clerkin Trio unpick and rethread myriad 90’s DIY tropes on an undeniably genius new mini album that takes the brittle, asymmetric pop of Pram, Stereolab’s orchestral arrangements, A.R. Kane’s penchant for straight looped-Amen-dreampop, and drape it with esoteric and uncomproimisingly modern chamber jazz and baroque folk baubles that are just impossible not to fall deeply in love with.

Aye that title track is an instant wonder, and shares a 90’s undercurrent with the more dubwise ‘World in Delay’, where echoes of Laika’s hybrid vibrations surface to transport us to a different time. ‘Marble Walls’, meantime, manages to remind us of both Broadcast’s ‘Tears In The Typing Pool’ and Stereolab’s 'Cybele's Reverie', all sweeping orchestral flourishes urged by a daydreamy, bubbling rhythm. 

The rest catches them in measuredly introspective mode, tidily drifting along streams of ferric hiss, rippling marimba and accordion into a hazy fantasy like Don Cherry meets A.R. Kane on the downbeat slunk of ‘Brigstow’, and folding a lute riff into loopy origami on the glorious, pastoral fade to close of ‘Once Again’. 

Stunner.
items._cn_summary: 塔拉·克莱尔金三重奏来自布里斯托尔，这张三十分钟的迷你专辑融合了民谣爵士、古典室内乐、梦幻流行与巴洛克民谣元素。乐队以九十年代DIY美学为底色，融入Stereolab式的管弦乐编排、A.R. Kane式的循环碎拍和Broadcast式的梦幻质感，同时加入马林巴、手风琴和鲁特琴等原声乐器，营造出带有磁带嘶声质感的室内爵士声响。作品在梦幻流行与当代古典之间游走，既有沉稳的内省气质，也有灵动的器乐编排，呈现出对九十年代实验独立音乐传统的重新编织。伦敦独立厂牌World of Echo发行，整体定位偏向氛围化与折衷主义的跨类型融合。

items.body:
Writing around and through improvisations he made with his Berlin-based cast of collaborators, Fabian Altstötter looks to Scott Walker and David Sylvian to guide 'Sustained', singing poetically over sparse, somber instrumentation.

Putting yourself up against Walker and Sylvian is a high bar that requires an advanced level of skill, but Altstötter's been at this for a minute; on his third solo full-length, he's as limber and unguarded as he needs to be, able to tenderly recite his words over surprisingly stripped-down productions. Because it would be almost too easy to over egg the pudding here - clearly, Altstötter is not only surrounded by friends who can really play (Roomer's Ronja Schößler helps with the songwriting and plays guitar and flute, Ralph Heidel plays brass and woodwind and Andy Aquarius handles the harp), but he has electronic options open to him that could, potentially, capsize the entire project. 

So the minimalist qualities of 'Sustained' are remarkable, then. Check 'Tell this Lover', that's reduced without sounding as if it's trying to make a big deal of it. The piano, bass and woodwind are clipped down to provide a rhythm, and although Altstötter's voice isn't as powerful as Sylvians or as unforgettable as Walker's, it drapes over the breathy, swingy sounds like silk. When Aquarius's harp enters the frame, it's like a crack of light in a dark room. Similarly, Altstötter's duet with Schößler, 'Again', is characterized by its tenderness and its unusually palette of sounds - the flutes that arrive in the third act, breezing through grumbling distortions and chugging guitars. Very nice.

items.body:
Toronto-based brothers Kevin and Patrick Cahill return to Death Is Not The End with another set of introspective folk-inspired instrumentals.

They might play nylon strung guitar and make what's in all respects "folk" music, but East of the Valley Blues don't draw from the expected sources, balancing out their interest in Americana with an understanding of music from across the world that genuinely widens their perspective. So their percussive opener 'Sitting in the Poem' can swerve utterly fluidly from serpentine Tuareg-inspired riffage to Fahey-esque fingerstyle and you barely notice it. And 'The Spider Underneath' can sound utterly outside the timeline, playing like an extended post-rock jam recorded in a basement in North Africa.

Taking one side of the stereo spectrum each, the brothers play off each other perfectly, leaving us to fill in the gaps. And they peak on the brilliant 'Like Fitzcarraldo', seemingly blending South American styles and plodding rock - no need to tug a steamboat over a mountain though, right? Or play Enrico Caruso in the Amazon.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由多伦多兄弟组合East of the Valley Blues创作，以尼龙弦吉他为核心乐器，呈现内省风格的器乐作品。音乐虽以民谣为根基，却广泛汲取世界音乐养分：开篇曲在图阿雷格风格的蛇形riff与Fahey式指弹间自由切换，另一首作品带有北非地下室后摇滚即兴的质感。双人各占据一侧声场，形成互补对话。专辑在美洲民谣、北非与南美音乐元素之间搭建桥梁，呈现出跨文化融合的探索意识，偏向实验性的世界音乐融合路线。发行厂牌Death Is Not The End为小型独立厂牌，整体定位偏向小众器乐与跨界民谣领域。

items.body:
Deep club modernist Sa Pa mints his own new label, Dub Techno For Life, with four top drawer cuts of textured, strident pressure tipped FFO classic Chain Reaction x Short Span.

Since 2015 Sa Pa has carved a heads-down path between techno, proper, and its conceptual adjuncts in ambient and sound designer atmospheres, most recently on Short Span and Astral Industries. Now taking matters into his own hands, the ‘Girls on Tour EP’ squares up his most robust club material alongside more experimental urges for a definitive self-portrait displaying a fine spectrum of strengths. 

The four tunes clearly speak to his diversity within a theme, checking for a firm touchstone in Andreas Tilliander aka Mokira with the 10 mins of rolling, claggy heft to ‘Mokira Ultra Dub’, unshelving his 2016 rework for deep ’26 ‘floors, alongside the puckered elegance of ‘Waiting For You’, harking to roots in Teutonic house minimalism, whereas the B-side attends to grubbier urges in the bittersweet, sludgy budge of ‘Modular System’, and lusher, abstract feels on the Actress or Rezzett-esque whorl of ‘World Saving Banger’.
items._cn_summary: Sa Pa的首张EP在其自创厂牌Dub Techno For Life发行，收录四首深俱乐部现代主义风格的dub techno作品。音乐扎根于经典的Chain Reaction式dub techno脉络，融合声音设计与氛围化质感，展现出在Techno与Ambient之间的独特路径。A面以厚重的滚动律动和极简主义优雅为主线，B面则偏向更粗糙、抽象的情绪表达，呼应Actress与Rezzett等人的实验电子美学。作为独立地下厂牌发行，作品兼具俱乐部实用性与实验探索性，但整体仍以舞曲功能性为核心，在声音设计的先锋性上有一定局限。

items.body:
Brassy, in-the-pocket, big band Afrobeat-jazz swag by 13-piece Hungarian ensemble, Hakumba.

“Written in a one week jam session retreat in the Hungarian countryside, and recorded at one of the highest peaks of Hungary after a year of global touring, The Garden becomes an amalgamation of the band's personal and artistic experiences. The material conveys a more jazzier approach, with complex harmonies, and an almost cinematic, dreamlike atmosphere, somewhat distancing from (but not completely forgetting) the previously emphasized, dance-oriented Afro- and Latino roots. Song for Ramon serves as the EP’s emotional climax inspired by the passing of a close friend and local underground chef pioneer.

Formed in 2019 in Budapest, Hakumba is a staple of the Hungarian festival circuit, with a growing international presence (SXSW London, SHIP, PIN Music Showcase). They’ve recently finished a tour in Australia this January.

The groove-driven ensemble blends afrobeat, jazz, and various strands of world music into a sound that is both rhythmically powerful and harmonically adventurous. With an eleven-piece lineup featuring an expansive horn section, multiple vocalists, percussion, and keys, the band moves effortlessly between dancefloor energy and more intricate, jazz-influenced musical ideas. Like the band’s previous album, the EP was again recorded, mixed, and mastered by András Weil, the producer behind The Qualitons, the only hungarian band ever performed Live at KEXP. This continuity preserves Hakumba’s recognizable sonic identity while giving space for new colors and more complex musical ideas to emerge.”
items._cn_summary: 匈牙利十三人乐团 Hakumba 的专辑《The Garden》，融合非洲节拍、爵士与拉丁音乐传统，以大乐队编制呈现复杂和声与电影化的梦境氛围。作品于匈牙利乡村的一周即兴创作后录制于该国高山地区，延续了乐队兼具舞曲能量与爵士深度的风格。铜管声部、多位人声、打击乐与键盘构成丰富的声场层次，部分曲目带有追忆逝友的情感色彩。乐评整体持正面评价，指出其跨类型融合的特征，但音乐仍偏向舞曲导向的世界音乐融合，实验性与前卫色彩有限。

items.body:
Enigmatic golden-era 4AD act Swallow reissue their first two albums from 1992 - Blow & Blowback - as an expanded double pack, 'Blown'.

"A chance for shoegaze fans to discover this forgotten gem from the 4AD catalogue, Blown is an essential but underrated body of work embracing the genre’s signature atmospheric layering of fuzzy guitar textures, accompanied by Louise Trehy’s beautiful and haunting vocals, creating hazy waves and swirls of luscious noise.

Swallow was formed by Louise Trehy and Mike Mason in London in the early 90’s, signed by Ivo Watts-Russell after receiving 4-song demo tape by post. Blow was originally released in July 1992, followed by Blowback in autumn of the same year featuring new mixes and overdubs and released as a limited CDEP that quickly fell out of print, known only to the most fervent 4AD fans. Swallow parted ways with 4AD shortly after the release of Blowback, but their brief period with the label has been outlived by this cornerstone dream-pop classic which has until now been obscured by the mists of time and memory.

With Blown, Swallow are reintroduced as an important force in the 4AD canon and the shoegaze genre, alongside their more well-known counterparts. The songs of Blown have been reconstructed from the original 24 track tape recordings and remixed. It has been freshly remastered by Anne Taegart at Dubplates and Mastering Berlin and lovingly presented in a brand-new package designed by longtime supporter Chris Bigg (v23) based on the original design by Vaughn Oliver.

Louise Trehy and Mike Mason met in early 90’s Camberwell, London. Both were deeply involved with the independent music scene of the time; Louise co-founded Setanta Records (home of The Divine Comedy, Edwyn Collins and Into Paradise with whom Mike would occasionally play), and Mike traversed between bike courier, video director, and lighting designer for Spacemen 3, Slowdive, Spiritualized, Curve and Chapterhouse. Prompted by Louise, they started writing songs together, drawing inspiration from a healthy mix of sources: CAN, noise, post-punk, and American forces of nature like Captain Beefheart and Butthole Surfers. Their first songs quickly surfaced and were recorded onto a Tascam 4-track portastudio. Louise posted the four-song demo to Ivo Watts-Russell who signed them to 4AD, sight unseen.

With the task of finishing their first record, the pair borrowed guitars from Tom Greenhalgh of the Mekons and they decamped to record at Edinburgh’s Palladium Studios and later, Blackwing in London. John Fryer was enlisted to produce (right off handling Nine Inch Nails’ 1989 record Pretty Hate Machine), utilizing Eventide Harmonizers (a Cocteau Twins staple) to provide the band’s lush, ethereal dazzle.

Blow would be released in July of 1992, and arrived in a sleeve designed by Vaughan Oliver (v23). Subsequently, they did a handful of support gigs with Bob Mould’s post-Hüsker Dü project Sugar and American shoegaze peers Medicine to promote the album across the UK. Contemporary reviews of Blow would unimaginatively make much of the 4AD and Cocteau’s connections. But with the music press’ attention later shifted to the Nirvana explosion of underground American bands, it was difficult for the album to get much attention.

Though, in the end, the band found the finished album different than they imagined it would sound. Feeling as though their initial ideas had been lost in the production, they petitioned Ivo to re-record parts of the album; he suggested they remix the tracks as they wished, instead. New mixes and overdubs resulted in dissonant and ambient versions closer to the band’s intentions, released as Blowback in the autumn of 1992. Sadly, expectations, hopes, and shifting priorities from both Ivo and the band led to Swallow’s departure from 4AD shortly after the release of Blowback.

Swallow pressed on and were invited to play a ten date UK tour with Mazzy Star. It was Mazzy Star who recommended Geoff Travis sign the band to his label Rough Trade in late 1993. Mike and Louise’s only release for the label was the 1994 Hush EP — recorded at home and more stripped back than the band’s previous releases, the release allowed the songs to stand ahead of their production for the first time. The full Hush session recordings would ultimately be released digitally in 2009."
items._cn_summary: Swallow是90年代初4AD厂牌旗下的shoegaze/dream-pop乐队，由Louise Trehy与Mike Mason创立。这张合辑重新发行了他们1992年的两张专辑《Blow》与《Blowback》。音乐风格以朦胧的吉他音墙、Loise Trehy空灵飘渺的人声为核心，融合了post-punk噪音元素与实验性制作手法，制作人John Fryer运用Eventide Harmonizer营造出Cocteau Twins式的迷幻氛围。乐队受到CAN、Captain Beefheart、Butthole Surfers等噪音与实验摇滚影响，加上4AD厂牌的暗潮美学传统，使其音乐在shoegaze范畴中带有较强的暗色与实验色彩。与Spacemen 3、Spiritualized、Curve等乐队的演出关联也强化了其地下独立音乐血统。整体属于post-punk/shoegaze交界地带，对暗潮与实验音乐爱好者具有一定吸引力。

items.body:
PT Musik (fka Puto Tito) epitomises Príncipe’s brand of rugged but melancholic batida on a standout new album dripping with piquant hooks and puckered grooves set to travel far beyond his Lisbon base.

One of the many joys of following Príncipe is hearing its artists grow over the years, as with Domingos Aleixo’s shifts from a bare-boned but vividly colourful 2019 debut ‘Carregando A Vida Atrás Das Costas’, to the notably lusher, more romantic harmonies of the ‘Não Sou Perfito’ 7”, which introduced his name change in 2021.The confident swagger and shrug-it-off sentiments ramps up on his second LP ‘Consumação’, featuring eight cuts that amount to a properly charming self-portrait of an artist coming into his own.

The blend of reflective melody and variegated, seductive and then urgent rhythms that has kept us all rapt to Príncipe is in ideal effect on this one. Themes of broken relationships, loneliness and navigating life’s travails prompt PT to his strongest work, manifest in a strong grasp of expressive, extended melody and breezy vibes that transcends language and speaks directly to both dancing bodies and dreamy minds.

Hooks are bitter-sweet, edged with a tang of heightened emotional maturity from tarraxho opener ’Nha Budjura’ thru a sentimental fave ‘Hot Girl’ that first appeared on 2020’s ‘Verão Dark Hope’ comp, and now closes the LP with a glimpse of their former self. In between, they serve the club with proper orders of sinuous breeziness on ‘Lembranças’ and ‘Leave me Alone’, plus the needling heat of ‘Movimento’, reserving the most poignant moment to the ‘90s R&B soul-inflected ’Não Acredito’ and elegant, dusky ambiguity of ‘Me Suga’ with minor key harpsichord and pitch-bent leads bound to burrow into memory.
items._cn_summary: PT Musik（前身为Puto Tito）来自里斯本的Príncipe厂牌，以batida和tarraxho风格为基础，将电子节奏与非洲散居音乐传统相融合。专辑《Consumação》在俱乐部舞曲框架中融入内省旋律、R&B灵魂元素与复古拨弦古钢琴声响，主题涉及孤独与情感创伤。整体制作保持了Príncipe厂牌一贯的电子世界观，节奏层丰富多变，但在实验性和前卫性上并未大幅突破。葡萄牙里斯本并非该流派的中心地带，其非洲散居音乐文化视角为作品增添了独特的地缘色彩。

items.body:
Blackpool and Skam’s greaziest electro mutant coughs up an addendum to their first LP in decade with a side quest ,’Phasia’, that continues the B-movie misadventures of ‘Phocus’

‘Phasia’ feels like finding a near derelict - but actually open - video store on the backstreets on Blackpool (the bit where it gets really reel), and being granted access to the bit behind the chain curtains by a proprietor not dissimilar to the joke shop owner in The League of Gentlemen. Behind the rare blueys, video nasties and forbidden Chubby Brown section, lies a portal to ‘Phasia’; a wormhole into the high grade ’80s funk smut and fractalized memory reflux of VHS Head projected onto all walls and jacked into the nipples of local council bigwigs, the £1 burger bloke on his day off, and the likes of Lewis Jones and intrepid holidaymakers looking for summat a bit more exotic, y’know, for specialist tastes.

Between the neon sludge and brassy fanfare of opener ‘Locus’ and never-made-it-to-video-reverie ‘Phocus Trailer’, the cutting room floor offcuts of ‘Phocus’ make a highly entertaining album in their own right, swerving from the electro-jump-cuts of ‘Strange Food’ to screwed power-pop like Peter Gabriel on quaaludes in ‘Mouth Matte’, thru the heart-in-mouth romance of its title tune, the orchestral stab flashes of ‘Head Crimes’ to the briny tang of ‘Dream Peeping’, like some curdled Kate Bush, and killer drug chug of ‘Phocus’. Love it.
items._cn_summary: VHS Head来自英国布莱克浦，延续B级电影配乐式的低保真电子美学，在复古八十年代放克质感和碎裂化电子声响之间游走。专辑融合了电子跳切、扭曲的流行碎片、管弦乐片段和迷幻噪音元素，呈现出一种怀旧而怪诞的声景。整体制作带有明显的硬件质感和DIY实验倾向，从黑胶出租店式的氛围营造到曲目间的风格跳跃，展现了较强的概念性和叙事感。Skam厂牌为发行方，属英国独立电子厂牌，无主流降权。音乐风格偏向复古电子与实验声响的交叉地带，与暗潮或学院派前卫路线有距离，但对喜爱非主流电子、概念性制作和独特声景美学的听众而言具有吸引力。

items.body:
NDW stalwarts of Ata Tak & Pyrolator vintage reflect on Düsseldorf’s post-Kraut styles with a fine grasp of slippery chill-out sleaze and pungent downbeat waft.

 

"Marking its 25th anniversary, A Certain Frank's 'Nothing' stands as a quietly distinctive chapter in Düsseldorf’s post-Kraut electronic lineage – understated, atmospheric, and strikingly timeless. With this anniversary edition, Bureau B once again highlights a strand of German electronic music that exists between eras and categories. Carefully remastered and now pressed on vinyl for the first time, Nothing returns not as a relic, but as a work whose understated clarity continues to resonate – a testament to Bureau B’s ongoing dedication to preserving and recontextualising Germany’s experimental pop heritage."
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑来自杜塞尔多夫后Kraut电子音乐谱系，介于冷潮Chill-out与Downbeat氛围之间，与Ata Tak和Pyrolator等NDW前辈的脉络一脉相承。音乐呈现出低调、氛围化的电子声响特质，融合了松弛的down律动与实验性电子质感，具有较强的时代延续性。25周年纪念版由独立厂牌Bureau B再版，重新混音并首次以黑胶形式发行，体现了德国实验流行音乐遗产的整理与传承。整体音乐风格与实验电子、环境音乐及暗潮等审美取向较为契合，但作为再版作品，其原创性在当下语境中有所折损，且评论内容偏向新闻稿性质，深度有限。

items.body:
Beautiful, mystic trodders by Lee “Scratch” Perry for Cedric Myton, Congo Ashanti & Watty Burnett’s harmonious reggae vocal trio The Congos, including the wee radge packet’s Black Ark mixes.

All deriving from sessions for The Congo’s legendary debut ‘Heart of The Congos’ (1977), as issued on Perry’s Black Ark Studio-related label, Black Art, ‘Ark Of The Covenant’ best portrays the producer’s genius for innovative vocal and instrumental production that captures his performers’ spirits like few others. 

The A-side is a slice of roots heaven, framing The Congos’ swaying, layered harmonies in heat-melted chords and swollen bass, sealed within the Black Ark’s soft wooden resonance, while the original 7” B-side ‘Noah Sugar Pan’ swipes the vox into ether, revealing Perry’s treacly bass underfoot and his lysergic guitar finesse under the hood. 

Perhaps the biggest attraction, however, is Lee Perry’s Original Black Ark Mix, utterly haunted with duppied vocal refractions and phantasmic details in the air that really tickle susceptible souls and soles of feet.
items._cn_summary: 这张作品收录了Lee 'Scratch' Perry为The Congos制作的1977年Black Ark录音室时期素材，属于根源雷鬼范畴。Perry以传奇的Black Ark制作手法对雷鬼进行了大胆的声音实验，运用多层人声和声、回响深厚的贝斯线以及迷幻质感的吉他，营造出空灵、幽灵般的声响空间。整体在传统牙买加根源雷鬼的框架上融入了极具实验性的制作理念，人声折射与空间效果的处理展现出超越时代的前瞻性。属于世界音乐与实验制作交界的作品，对偏好先锋声响和异域文化视角的听众具有一定吸引力，但核心仍是雷鬼基底，与电子、前卫爵士等偏好领域的直接关联有限。

items.body:
Tapes touches bass(bins) with OG patrons Jahtari on a bevy of digi-dancehall party starters.

Big fun, this one! Back in his dub lane after the fruity flex of ‘Funk Plates Vol. 1’ (2023) for Disrupt’s adorable label, Jackson Bailey aka Tapes taps right into the label’s dub and chip tune tastes with a mix of full fat originals and 8-bit versions bound to put a big daft grin on red-eyed mugs. 

Stepping up nimbly strongback with dancehall croaker ‘Photos of my Frog’, riddled with sampled snippets of said snaps, she appears to weave in waviest traces of South African bubblegum top lines in the gummier bubble of ‘Cleat Skank’, replete with a saturated, bit-crushed version on the skweee tip.

Dung below he toes a darker dancehall line laden with killer snares, Gregorian ribbet and mystic melodies in ‘Ramp Up’ and the irresistible UK steppers momentum of a ‘Back Cramp’ licked up with frothiest choral vamps, whistles, and amphibian motifs that come squashed like King Tubby fucking with the OG Prince of Persia OST.
items._cn_summary: Tapes在Jahtari厂牌下发行了这张将数字dancehall、dub与8-bit芯片音乐融合的EP，并融入南非泡泡糖音乐元素。制作手法上运用了比特压缩、降采样等低保真实验性处理，参考了King Tubby的混音美学与Prince of Persia游戏原声的怀旧音色。整体定位偏向舞池派对场景，节奏驱动明显，UK steppers律动与舞蹈hall人声采样交织。独立小厂牌Jahtari一贯支持地下电子与dub场景，发行定位明确。音乐在电子制作与跨文化融合方面有一定新意，但实验性深度有限，更偏向趣味性与律动感而非前卫探索。

items.body:
Burial chases his ace remix of Luke Slater’s ‘Love’ with a redress of the UK techno legend’s L.B. Dub Corps.

Ironically enough, Slater’s very Burial-esque original is reframed as a fairly straight-playing, deep techno tune by the secretive south Londoner himself. Rising up on a beatific organ draught, and rolling out to shuffled hardcore 2-step break overlaid with Slater’s gauzy vox, the original clearly derives from a vein of UK rave spirit that has long perfused Burial’s catalogue.

The remix therefore perhaps falls slightly short of expectations, quite simply reducing the elements to a distant warehouse throb while stretching it out to twice the length, compressing and filtering the vox to an eyrie thizz and reserving the organ refrain to a elegiac coda. Will probably sound ace when munted, though.
items._cn_summary: Burial对英国techno传奇Luke Slater旗下L.B. Dub Corp项目进行混音再创作。原作融合管风琴音色、碎拍hardcore 2-step节奏与朦胧人声，散发浓厚的英国rave精神气质。混音版将核心元素精简为远距仓库式低频脉动，时长拉伸至原版两倍，对人声进行压缩滤波处理形成空灵感，管风琴旋律则被保留为挽歌式尾声。整体属于英国地下电子场景的跨界合作，在techno与UK bass传统之间寻找平衡点，但评论者认为混音版相对原作略显平淡，未能完全超越预期。

items.body:
Echospace Detroit’s Stephen Hitchell is at his most romantic, club-friendly and elemental on these effortless dub house glyders, newly remastered by Pole for posterity and optimal immersion

Originally issued on 12” in 2015 and hard-to-find ever since, ‘Lost Sequence’ is classic, archetypal Echospace tackle. The OG goes for 14 mins of strutting deep house groove swaddled in velvet-coated textures dubbed to the rafters and happy to hold its lane for the duration, adding extra layers of conga and crackling atmosphere as it proceeds. Hitchell’s Intrusion dub pitches the same elements in a spring weather system, drenching everything in fine mist of elemental FX and loosening the bass drum to a satisfyingly soggy slosh for 16 minutes of hypnotic bliss out.
items._cn_summary: 这张作品来自Echospace Detroit的Stephen Hitchell，以dub house为骨架，融合deep house的律动与dub的回响处理手法，呈现出绵长而沉浸的电子声响。专辑包含原版与Intrusion的dub混音版本，时长均在十四至十六分钟，结构松弛，层次在循环中缓慢堆叠，天鹅绒般的质感与crackling氛围交织，鼓点被刻意松解为绵软的slosh。整张作品偏向俱乐部场景的催眠式聆听体验，由Pole重新母带处理以提升沉浸感。作为电子音乐谱系中的氛围化dub house分支，它在音色深度与空间感上具有品质保障，但整体仍属于类型内的成熟创作，创新幅度有限。

items.artist: Mats Edén, Tellef Kvifte, Knut Kvifte Nesheim
items.excerpt: Mats Edén, Tellef Kvifte, Knut Kvifte Nesheim - Krota
items.body: Króta , the latest release on Norway's Taragot label, features a Swede and two Norwegians playing interpretations of mainly traditional tunes from their respective countries. Fiddler Mats Edén has long been involved in Swedish folk music, as a player, composer and teacher, and in the process exploring and integrating different musical styles and approaches. Tellef Kvifte was in the pioneering Norwegian crossover band Slinkombas in the 1970s and has continued to play a central role in Norwegian folk music, both as a musician and an academic. Most often heard playing the sjøfløyte , more widely known as a recorder, Kvifte has employed other instruments from outside the Norwegian tradition, in particular the saxophone and bagpipes. His son Knut Kvifte Nesheim , a drummer and composer, has also shown a determination to blur the lines between different musical genres, both in his solo and group projects. Króta by Edén/Kvifte/Nesheim trio It comes as no surprise then to find this trio offering a far from conventional take on the tunes they have chosen. While dance tunes may be the source of most of the material here, this feels more akin to chamber music; not that it is remotely classical in style, but in the sense it conveys of three players engrossed in a musically intimate conversation. This is not a performance appropriate for accompanying dancers but might instead be seen as an exploration of hidden possibilities of meaning in the music. In so doing it reveals some of its underlying mystery, including, perhaps, a darker side. Just as in an Ibsen play, where the surface bonhomie, jollity and social nicety can be hiding something more sinister, in Scandinavian dance music there are at times hints of a troublesome undercurrent below the surface. So the decision to open proceedings with “Fossgrimen,” a fiddle tune from Norway's Setesdal valley, is perhaps significant. A fossgrimen is a mythical creature, a kind of water-sprite living in waterfalls from whom fiddle-players were considered to have learned their skills and for that were not universally welcomed, with the fiddle considered to be the devil's instrument. Króta by Edén/Kvifte/Nesheim trio Tellef Kvifte takes the lead melody on most tracks but on the Swedish “Polska from Per Myhr,” having played a repeated introductory riff on the sjøfløyte, with Mats Edén providing an amorphous textural accompaniment below and Nesheim adding some quiet tinkling, it's Edén who introduces the tune on the fiddle with Kvifte proceeding to play in unison. It's a short track and almost as soon as it gets going things start to fragment and everything grind to a halt. Króta by Edén/Kvifte/Nesheim trio From the title of "Springar from Knut Nord-Juveli" we learn that it was taken from the repertoire of a renowned sjøfløyte player from Numedal, a valley in the east of Norway and is an appropriate feature for Tellef Kvifte. A springar is a Norwegian triple-beat dance whose three beats vary in length depending on which region of Norway the tune comes from. In this case the underlying pulse resembles that of a rhumba with each bar having two similar beats followed by a shorter one; but the melodic structure is unmistakably Norwegian with a motif being repeated, then the third time through it developing into a variation. Króta by Edén/Kvifte/Nesheim trio “På Siljan“ was taken from a collection of old Swedish tunes, but the version here is not so much an interpretation as a deconstruction of an item from the Swedish fiddle tradition. Beginning with Edén playing freely, seeking out the resonances of the fiddle through the gentle scraping of the strings with the bow, the tune eventually arrives quietly through the back door, carried by Kvifte on his sjøfløyte while Edén continues to improvise, along with Nesheim playing loosely around his kit. Tellef Kvifte pretty much sticks to the tune, a thread that runs through the track while the other two work around it, creating a rich sound texture, the listener being challenged to decide which is in front and which is behind. An adventurous and worthwhile endeavour which shows once again how traditional music can be not merely a legacy to uphold, but a catalyst for creativity.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张来自挪威小厂牌Taragot的斯堪的纳维亚民间音乐专辑，由一位瑞典小提琴手与两位挪威音乐家组成的三重奏演绎。三位音乐人均有跨流派探索背景，致力于模糊不同音乐类型的边界。专辑以挪威和瑞典传统舞曲为素材，但摒弃了舞蹈伴奏功能，转而呈现为类似室内乐的三人亲密对话。评论指出音乐表面之下暗藏不安的暗流，呼应易卜生戏剧中表面欢愉下的阴暗面。编曲手法上注重质感纹理和即兴碎片化处理，传统乐器如竖笛和小提琴被赋予非传统的表现方式。整体定位介于世界民间音乐、实验室内乐与当代古典之间，偏向有实验意识的跨界民乐听众。

items.body: After nine previous albums and a 25-year career at the forefront of world music, Lucas Santtana is fluent in the many genres of Brazilian music. His new project, Brasiliano , is a musical exploration of the languages of Brazil. With songs sung in Portuguese, French, English, Spanish, Occitan, Cape Verde Creole, and Tupy-Guarani, a Brazilian native language, Santtana has assembled guest lyricists and vocalists representing a range of musical and linguistic influences. The result is a warm and compelling musical treatise on the diverse cultural history of Brazil, expressed through the Brazilian variant of Portuguese, best described as Brasiliano. Returning to his roots, the opening cut and lead single “A história de nossa língua” features Gilberto Gil, a national treasure with whom Santtana worked early in his career. As the liner notes explain, Brasiliano , the language, is depicted in the song as a feminine character meeting other people (languages) on her travels, tracing the history of the language as an offshoot of Latin, including “Occitan, Celtic, Galician, Portuguese, Mozarabic, and others. The chorus features Indigenous words that are part of everyday Brazilian culture: Itapuã, Ipanema, Maracanã, Capoeira, etc.” This song acts as a sort of abstract for the dissertation to follow. Santtana and Gil call and respond over what has become the composer’s trademark mixture of detailed, layered, human-played instruments, including on this track violins and violas, piano, guitars, mellotron, and synths. Throughout the record, Santtana creates an inviting effect with a contemporary gloss, combined with the warm resonance of wood, drum skins, wire strings, sticks, bows, and voices. The album features a range of styles, from the lively party track “Ver meu povo se abraçar” to the convincing reggae of the second single, “Que seja um reggae”. With sophisticated songcraft and inspired arrangements, the songs remain inviting and accessible. Brasiliano by Lucas Santtana Fitting with the theme of the interrelationships among languages, Brasiliano is a celebration of international collaboration. For example, “Independência” features Karyna Gomes, a singer from Guinea-Bissau; Anglo-French performer Piers Faccini sings “Battre des ailes” accompanied by an appropriately French-sounding accordion; and popular Brazilian singer Flavia Coelho is featured on “Dans le sud feat”. The gentle “Strati di tempo” is the closest to Santtana’s earliest singer/guitarist style, with Italian star Dimartino taking the lead vocals. Brasiliano by Lucas Santtana Language is culture; so too are politics. And with the involvement of Gilberto Gill, who served as Minister of Culture in President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s government and was jailed and exiled for his political affiliations in the 1960s, it is no surprise that this album is overtly political. For example, on “Línguas Gerais,” French rapper Oxmo Puccino “speaks about colonization.” Continuing to quote from the liner notes, “Indigenous languages and cultures in South America were buried under European colonization.” Tainara Takua and Oxmo Puccino sing “Cocanha” in Occitan. Their music is part of a movement to prevent this endangered romance language from dying out. Like his popular previous recording O Paraíso (2023), which was concerned with the environment, Brasiliano is a concept album that explores the role of linguistics in culture. And like on O Paraíso , Santtana is never preachy. The high-minded intellectual roots of the project are made palatable by the creative and appealing music assembled to tell the story. It is a message of inclusion, collaboration, and the joy of our shared occupancy in this place and at this time. With many languages, many musical styles, and the artistry of many talented and effective musical partners, Brasiliano is a remarkable achievement in curation and musical skill with a compelling contemporary message.
items._cn_summary: 巴西音乐人Lucas Santtana的新专辑《Brasiliano》以音乐探索巴西多元语言文化为概念，曲目涵盖葡萄牙语、法语、英语、西班牙语、奥克语、佛得角克里奥尔语及土著图皮-瓜拉尼语等多语种演唱。专辑邀请包括Gilberto Gil在内的多位国际合作者，呈现文化交融与殖民历史的政治叙事。制作上以当代电子音色（合成器、mellotron）与原声乐器（小提琴、钢琴、吉他、手风琴）相结合，风格跨越雷鬼、民谣与世界节庆音乐。作为来自拉丁美洲的世界音乐作品，专辑具有独特的文化视角和跨语言合作模式，但整体仍偏向精致的当代世界音乐路线，在实验性和前卫声响探索方面深度有限。

items.body: Review by A Crimson Mellotron — There is something truly special about TesseracT's debut studio album 'One', released in 2011through Century Media Records, who had signed them just a year earlier. An almost decade-longdevelopment anticipates the release of this excellent studio album, as the band itself had startedout in 2003, with guitarists Acle Kahney and James Monteith experimenting with technical guitar workand posting various clips online that would gain them sufficient popularity. The current lineup ofthe band would take shape around 2009, which is very likely the moment in which the album 'One' hadbeen conceived as well. Predated by the EP 'Concealing Fate', which contains a six-part 27-minute-long suite (which appears in full on the album), 'One' impresses with an imminent, subtle, andgroovy sound that becomes unmistakable after some listening. Developing the so-called djent sound,the Meshuggah inspiration is not as obvious here as it is in bands like Periphery or Vildhjarta.The sound of TesseracT is zealously technical and rhythmically intense, but there is also aninherent accessibility to their music, which comes from the melodic vocal delivery of frontmanDaniel Tompkins. He does a fantastic job on 'One' and I can definitely see why this album had beenin the making for almost a decade - it is incredibly well-done, subtle and intense, explosivelyharsh when you least expect it to be, and pensive and melancholic when the guitar sounds become toooverwhelming. The balance between technical playing, pure songwriting and accessibility makes thisrecord not only an impressive debut from the Milton Keynes-based band, but also a signature releasefor the djent movement, at least in my view. A good example of songs that balance out the ambient-inspired sections with the dense and heavy prog playthroughs, are the opening track 'Lament', whichsets a beautifully epic tone to the record, and the shorter song 'April'. At the same time, trackslike 'Nascent' and 'Eden' impress with a dark, futuristic, and relentless sound that captures someof the band's most sophisticated arrangements and transitions, while the six-part epic 'ConcealingFate' is just brilliant and probably deserves a dedicated review of its own.No matter how familiar you are with the djent movement or with TesseracT's catalogue, their 2011debut album 'One' will surely blow your heads off with striking complexity and immaculate control,depicting an important step in the development of modern progressive metal.
items._cn_summary: TesseracT首张录音室专辑《One》是djent运动中的标志性作品，以技术性吉他演奏、复杂节奏结构和环境氛围段落著称。专辑在前卫金属框架内融入了ambient元素，平衡了技术演奏与旋律可听性，主唱Daniel Tompkins的旋律性演唱为沉重的器乐编排提供了呼吸空间。包含六部分史诗套曲《Concealing Fate》在内，专辑展示了多层次编曲与情绪起伏的掌控力。作为前卫金属子流派的代表，作品具有一定的实验性和跨界融合意识，但整体仍以金属为核心，对偏好纯实验、前卫爵士或电子音乐的听众而言，跨入门槛较高。厂牌Century Media为独立金属厂牌，不涉及主流降权。

items.body: Review by Aussie-Byrd-Brother — A firecracker of an instrumental album, `Riot' is the 2012 debut (and sole release to date) from young Indonesian band Tohpati Bertiga. Formed around guitarist Tohpati Ario Hutomo, bassist Indro Hardjodikor - both previously involved with eclectic instrumentalists SimakDialog - and drummer Adityo Wibowo, the exceptionally talented trio deliver fiery and energetic prog/jazz rock with elements of funk, fusion and ethnic flavours.Recording the album live in the studio with only minimal touch-ups means the group capture a real spontaneity and urgency, and they infect their constantly up-tempo pieces with a true liveliness, even a touch of playfulness. The ten tracks on offer are all tightly written, nimble arrangements, but also frequently hold passages for the band to improvise and jam, usually in the way of mangled, molten-fuelled guitar soloing, rapid-fire bass salvos and thrashing drum spasms.Opener `Unload' instantly blasts with precision riffing and a stuttering metallic heaviness, the tiniest traces of King Crimson's `Red' creeping in. `Middle East' hypnotises with its twisting turns, the improv-heavy `Pay Attention's sly funk and immersive jazz soundscapes beg you to do just that (you try ignoring the insane bass soloing in it!), and `Rock Camp' free-wheels with boogie and bluesy struts before a twitchy mental breakdown.`Lost in Space' cools things down for an introspective and mysterious chill-out, `Bertiga' reminds of the genre-blending cheerful eclecticism and playfulness of Seventies group Kraan. `Robot Disco' melts quirky electronics into spastic metal attacks, and the bouncy and jubilant `I Feel Fine' turns out to be the biggest ear-worm of the lot of them, sure to have your foot tapping in no time!While all the compositions showcase the expressive, fluid and dynamic skills of the trio, `Riot' never comes across as mere show-off displays or inane noodling, and it's as far from deadly-serious, stuffy jazz-fusion as possible. The album is carried by the fire, passion and excitement that only youth can bring, and it even holds a strong melodicism that makes it approachable for listeners who may not usually have the patience for an all-instrumental disc.Hopefully the band didn't burn themselves out completely with this effort and deliver a follow-up in the future!Four stars.
items._cn_summary: 印尼三重奏乐队Tohpati Bertiga于2012年发行的首张专辑《Riot》，由吉他手、贝斯手与鼓手组成，定位为爵士摇滚融合。以现场录音方式捕捉即兴火花，融合前卫摇滚、爵士、疯克与世界民族音乐元素，节奏紧凑，充满年轻乐手的热情与张力。吉他独奏炽热奔放，贝斯线条迅捷密集，鼓击强劲多变，曲目在精密编排与自由即兴间游走，融入印尼本土民族色彩，少量电子声响出现在个别段落中。作为东南亚地区的独立制作，该专辑展现出介于学院爵士融合与世界音乐之间的跨文化气质，适合对跨界融合音乐感兴趣且能接受传统爵士摇滚语言的听众。

items.body: Review by The Progolyte — Wow, what a hidden gem! Capitolo 6 was one of the countless Italian bands from this period who flirted with progressive rock, but for me, I'd say they're one of the finest examples of a Rock Progressivo Italiano band that just never got its footing while active and never got the praise it deserves years later. The one album they did make, Frutti Per Kagua, is an amazing compilation of engaging jams, technical progressive rock, and twinges of jazz rock, all mixed in with a heavy edge that echoes what the band's English counterparts were doing at the same time. I noticed a very clear similarity to Jumbo, not only musically but vocally as well. Their singer, Riccardo Bartolotti (who also does some guitar and flute here and there), has that same raspy and intense quality that catches your ear whenever you listen to Alvaro Fella sing on a Jumbo album. On the topic of the personnel, Jimmy Santerini plays keyboards and does some singing parts, Lorenzo Donati does the drumming and is also listed as helping with the vocals, Maurizio Romani plays the bass, and Loriano Berti performs as the band's saxophonist and flutist. The record opens with the phenomenal twenty-minute-long title track, which is my favorite piece on the whole record and contains some extremely interesting and well-put-together music. It's a fascinating mix of bluesy, guitar-heavy rock music, blissful folk compositions, emotionally driving melodies and jamming and is overall a great experience that has a great sense of direction and identity. It really goes to show how far this group could've gone if they had gotten the recognition they deserved. Side two has the other three tracks, none of which are quite as long but generally have a good frame for length. The energy on side one continues as each piece is full of captivating moments of pure power and very dynamic material that truly breathes and flows greatly. The fast-paced, almost jazz fusion-like rhythms are only contrasted by the calming seas of acoustic material, but overall the music here is very much on the electric side of things. Overall, it's all very strong and a great representation of Rock Progressivo Italiano at its core, with both charming and grittier tones of the scene. In conclusion, I would highly recommend this band for anyone wanting to expand their knowledge on the map of Italian prog. It's very reminiscent of some of the classics while also feeling fresh and fun. It may not be an absolute essential, but to me it is deserving of a very strong 4.25/5.
items._cn_summary: Capitolo 6是1972年意大利摇滚场景中的隐藏宝藏，作品融合了技术性前卫摇滚、爵士摇滚、民谣段落与蓝调吉他摇滚等多种元素，呈现出典型的意大利前卫摇滚风貌。开场二十分钟同名曲是全作核心，结构庞大，兼具蓝调式的厚重吉他、放克律动与民谣的舒缓段落，动静态对比鲜明。第二面收录三首较短曲目，延续了高速爵士融合节奏与原声平静段落的交替，整体偏向电气化表达。乐队主唱Riccardo Bartolotti沙哑而富张力的嗓音与意大利前辈乐队Jumbo有相似之处，乐手配置涵盖键盘、萨克斯、长笛与贝斯，演奏具备一定技术水准。作为小众意大利厂牌发行的RPI作品，它既继承了经典时期的传统，又有自身的探索空间，适合希望拓展意大利前卫摇滚版图的听众。

items.body: Justin Taylor’s Clavecin XX presents an intriguing selection of solo and ensemble works by Bartók, Françaix, Górecki, Poulenc, and Manuel de Falla, placing a traditionally antiquated instrument squarely in a modern context. For this recording, Taylor utilizes a 1970s harpsichord by Anthony Sidey that hybridizes elements from 1920s Pleyels with much earlier models. This versatility, the artist notes, allowed him to rely on a single instrument throughout the diverse recital. Indeed, the Sidey instrument’s profile encompasses an array of personalities and sonorities that are brilliantly unveiled across the album. Clavecin XX Amazon Presto Apple Referencing Baroque forms like the Toccata and Minuet, Jean Françaix’s Concerto features a distinctive tonal language that places the harpsichord in a curious perspective. Deriving its energy from Taylor’s full-bodied tremolos, Toccata I is further animated by piquant string pizzicatos that add a sprightly, balletic quality. Sharing a similar texture but adopting a diametrically opposed, lyrical profile, Toccata II allows the keyboardist to trace horizontal lines with a pleasing legato, its fluidity highlighting refreshing harmonic progressions. Demonstrating the chameleon-like quality of the instrument, Taylor shines in the Minuet. Here, the harpsichord occasionally resembles a dulcimer or a Japanese koto, bringing a fitting dimension to a multifaceted compositional language steeped in Impressionism, cinema, and dance. Serving as a stark departure from the preceding charm, the selection by Henryk Górecki is deeply stimulating in how its two movements employ repetitional minimalism to cast the harpsichord in strikingly different lights. Taylor’s even-keeled perpetuum mobile in the Allegro molto is insistent, clashing unapologetically with the equally stubborn, static ensemble part. The resulting sonority is mechanical, bordering on the computerized. Driven by relentless chords, the subsequent Vivace marcatissimo builds profound tension. The performers do a remarkable job maintaining metronomic precision, molding a conflict that eventually comes to a head as spectacular harmonic collisions evolve into a frenetic sonic assault—an effect most certainly intended given the music’s inherent angst. While Manuel de Falla’s selection injects rhythmic vitality into the program, Francis Poulenc‘s Concert champêtre stands out for its high-spirited, imaginative execution. Written for Wanda Landowska (an artist Taylor cites as a major inspiration), the concerto operates in a Neo-Baroque style. Conjuring stately authority in their slow introduction, the orchestra sets the stage for the keyboardist to bring elegant liveliness to the Allegro section. The Finale is arguably the most engaging movement due to its sheer eclecticism. Launching as a virtuosic Gigue, it quickly diversifies to encompass hints of improvisation, a march, and elements drawn from Romantic and Neo-Romantic symphonies. Adapting to this complex structure admirably, the performers ensure no particular reference feels contrived or out of place. In this work, as in the other concertos, the Orchestre National de Lille under Chloé Dufresne is an attentive partner, articulating the clever counterpoint clearly while never overshadowing the harpsichord. Justin Taylor. Photo © Jean-Baptiste Millot. Turning to the solo works, the opening selection from Bartók‘s Mikrokosmos serves as a brief but wonderfully rendered introduction, establishing the character of the entire program through its interplay between consonance and dissonance. Taylor’s precise articulation gives the notes ample space to resonate, allowing listeners to appreciate them individually while sympathetic resonances beautifully mingle. Paying homage to György Ligeti’s landmark harpsichord work Continuum (which famously transforms the instrument into an ominous, persistent buzz), Stéphane Gassot’s Bluesinuum offers a gentler take. Although it references a similar trill-like texture in its middle section, Gassot’s approach is notably more subdued. Taylor’s bluesy rhythms possess both snap and fluidity, while occasional lower-register rumbles introduce a welcome playfulness to the mix. Concluding the album is a familiar tune: Scott Joplin’s Maple Leaf Rag. While the execution is solid and the artist’s transcription remains faithful to the original, hearing this piece on a harpsichord proves difficult to digest. The timbre of the instrument simply does not suit the repertoire, transforming the music’s inherent jauntiness into something rather heavy and labored. Perhaps this iconic rag is best left to its intended medium, the piano. Taylor’s interview in the liner notes portrays him as a well-spoken, meticulous musician who has invested significant research into his repertoire prior to performance. With the exception of the final track, this curation stands as an engaging testament to the harpsichord’s vast capabilities well beyond its traditional Baroque boundaries. Though not all the pieces make for easy listening, Taylor undeniably maximizes the instrument’s technical and musical capacity. items._cn_summary: 这张专辑汇集了二十世纪作曲家为羽管键琴创作的作品，涵盖戈雷茨基的极简主义重复结构、法兰西的新巴洛克语言、普朗克受旺达·兰多芙丝卡启发的协奏曲，以及法雅的西班牙舞曲元素。演奏者使用一把1970年代由安东尼·西迪制作的混合式羽管键琴，将传统乐器置于现代语境中，展现其多变的音色个性——从印象派、舞蹈性节奏到近乎电子化的机械音响。戈雷茨基段落中持续运动的固定音型与静态合奏的对抗，呈现出一定程度的实验色彩。整体定位为当代学院派古典音乐，对关注现代作曲技法与跨风格融合的听众具有参考价值，但在先锋性和声音探索上仍偏向保守。

items.body: With the cards you hold But who’s on trial Carve their names Declare your crimes Since we last checked in, Brooklyn-bred noise rock quartet Clone have been hard at work, honing their craft on stage and in the studio. The band has just returned from a short stint on the road and offers up a blistering video for the single “Care to Try?” from their EP of the same name, which was released in October of last year. “Care to Try?” follows up the band’s debut album CL.1, released in 2024. “Care to Try?” is a powerful anthem of resistance, targeting and taunting the current political administration in the USA with biting lyrics and hard-hitting, guitar-driven discord. Opening with short burst of feedback and a catchy, yet incisive melody, the track quickly takes hold and goes straight for the jugular, with vocalist LG Galleon seething and shouting lyrics of rebellion above the din to dizzying effect. Shades of bands such as Live Skull, Naked Raygun, The Chameleons, and Killing Joke can be heard throughout the track, which eventually explodes into a cacophonous, scorched-earth coda that commands reflection and action. Filmed and colored by Devan Davies and edited by Galleon, the video for “Care to Try?” perfectly reflects the song’s fiery intent. “With their second go-around things just seem even more hopeless than before,” adds Galleon, “and this video tries to capture he frustration of an ever increasing world gone mad.” Check out the track and video below, and be sure to catch the band live this Thursday at Berlin Under A in NYC. More dates below. Clone Tour Dates June 4 — NYC — Berlin under A June 5 — San Juan, PR — El Local en Santurce June 6 — San Juan, PR — Club 77 July 5 — Brooklyn, NY — Mama Tried Follow Clone: Linktree Bandcamp Instagram Spotify The post New York Quartet Clone Evoke Political Dissonance and Fury in “Care to Try?” appeared first on Post-Punk.com.
items._cn_summary: Clone是来自布鲁克林的噪音摇滚四人组，单曲"Care to Try?"延续了后朋克的粗粝质感与政治张力。作品以失真反馈开篇，吉他驱动的尖锐旋律配合主唱LG Galleon愤怒的呐喊，形成具有攻击性的声墙。曲末以破坏性极强的噪音尾声收束，制造出焦土般的听觉冲击。乐队在风格上受到Live Skull、The Chameleons、Killing Joke等经典后朋克/噪音摇滚乐队的影响，定位介于后朋克与硬核噪音之间，具有一定的实验性但整体仍属类型化框架内的作品。歌词直指当前美国政治环境，传达抵抗与不满情绪，MV的视觉风格与歌曲气质保持一致。作为独立厂牌发行的地下乐队作品，具有一定的小众属性。

items.body: When the fields of the cross were burning Our paths would go their separate ways Somehow we were always learning Learning from our own mistakes DETOXi’s In Laughter carries the strange charge of unfinished business: a song born in the pandemic years, finally given its full second life. Southern California deathrock has always known how to turn damage into drama, but this track carries itself with a bruised grandeur that feels earned, shaped by absence, distance, and the weird ache of art left suspended when the world stopped mid-sentence. Musically, the song feels cut from a generous, high-hearted lineage. There is the romantic sweep of The Cult, the broad reach of Midnight Oil, the open-road lift of Big Country, the hard tension of Killing Joke, and a flash of Aztec Camera’s bittersweet clarity in the way melody and feeling are allowed to meet head-on. Jennings sings straight into a memory with a killer anthemic chorus, while the band pushes forward with a handsome urgency, turning grief into motion and ultimately release. Lyrically, In Laughter traces a relationship marked by fear, separation, and unresolved longing, returning again and again to the idea that love survives through joy rather than pain. Burning fields, graves, frozen time, and repeated invitations give the song the feeling of a letter written after the worst has already happened, when tenderness becomes the last brave act left. Director Braedon Roller treats the performance video like a transmission from a band interrupted by history, then summoned back by the force of unfinished feeling. “For this project, I wanted to borrow stylistically from David Lynch’s Blue Velvet,” says Roller. “I’ve always been struck by the candy-colored clown scene and thought that lighting and mood would be perfect inspiration for a music video. I also pulled from films like [Robert Eggers’] The VVitch and…Nosferatu: dark, desaturated imagery living in blue and orange tones. The song has this haunting beauty to it, and I wanted to capture that while really focusing on the emotion of the performance. One technique I like to use is having the singer perform in double time while overcranking the camera, then slowing the footage down in post so the performance lands perfectly on tempo. It creates this strange, hypnotic effect that felt right for this song. The video was filmed across two separate nights, over 4 years, and the edit was incredibly labor-intensive, but I’m really proud of how it turned out.” Watch the video for In Laughter below: The backstory of the band has the cruel timing of a rock-and-roll fable. DETOXi played the vinyl release show for their debut album, First Flesh, on Leap Year Day in 2020, only days before record stores and venues closed, putting the band’s momentum into a deep freeze. During the uncertainty that followed, they kept recording, releasing the In Laughter EP in March 2021 and beginning work on a video for the title track. Then life scattered the pieces: Derek Jennings relocated to Portland, Oscar Estrada and John Crerar started HEAD CUT, and Matt Barks turned his focus toward projects outside music. DETOXi Still, In Laughter kept moving. DJs found it. Fans passed it around. Social media did its strange little underground magic trick, carrying the song into new circles while longtime listeners kept asking when DETOXi might return to the stage. Listen to In Laughter below and order the EP here. In Laughter EP by DETOXI And DETOXi return to the stage Friday, June 26, for their first show since the pandemic, celebrating Crerar’s 50th birthday at Vaquero y Mar in Ventura, California…the same venue where they last played before lockdown. The lineup brings together their earlier incarnation Maask, HEAD CUT, Guilty Strangers, and Dusk At Midnight. For DETOXi, the circle closes with feedback, friendship, and laughter carrying through the wreckage. Get tickets to the show here. items.body: This is my house I’m pretty sure Or did I turn the wrong way at the corner store? There are few things more quietly terrifying than realizing a place meant to hold us no longer seems to know us. A home can turn uncanny without changing shape: the same walls, the same rooms, the same door, and yet the air feels wrong. A party can become alien in an instant. A familiar street can suddenly feel like a wrong turn. Sometimes the most frightening estrangement is not from other people, but from our own certainty — that small internal rupture when memory, perception, and instinct stop agreeing with one another. That uneasy threshold is where Berlin-based quartet Agatha is Dead! place their new single “Strangers.” Taken from their forthcoming debut album Concrete, due out on September 11, the track is a study in dissociation, displacement, and the peculiar horror of feeling locked out of a life that should belong to you. “Strangers” opens with a danceable drum beat and a thick, softly carried shadow-laced bass groove, quickly joined by a rubbery, reverbed guitar figure that glints like a melody half-remembered. It almost masquerades as a piano hook: bright, repetitive, and singable, but with enough coldness in its edges to keep the mood unsettled. There is a trace of the icy, Eastern European post-punk guitar language popularized by acts like Molchat Doma, but Agatha is Dead! bend that familiar vocabulary into something more elastic, melodic, and contemporary. The result is a sound stripped down to its essentials without feeling nostalgic for its own sake. When the vocals enter, roughly half a minute in, they arrive controlled and rhythmic, carrying a poetic cadence with a sighing edge. Rather than pushing the song into melodrama, the performance tightens the tension: the melody becomes more insistent, the groove more infectious, and the chorus gradually takes on an anthemic charge. By the time the central cry of “strangers in my house” rises into view, the track has turned paranoia into a hook — something intimate, frightening, and strangely cathartic. Lyrically, “Strangers” follows a narrator trying to re-enter what should be their own space, only to find every sign of belonging destabilized. The house is familiar, or at least it should be. The faces are not. The details have shifted. The mind keeps searching for a rational explanation — a wrong turn, a misplaced key, a simple mistake — but the deeper dread is that something has gone wrong in perception itself. The refrain’s fear of being “locked me out” lands less like a literal complaint than a plea to return to the self. At around the 2:45 mark, the song shifts into a slower, eerier passage, letting the anguish breathe before the rhythm gathers itself again for the final stretch. It is here that the track’s sense of domestic unease becomes something larger: a fear of being made foreign in your own body, your own memory, your own home. And for anyone who has experienced tragedy and turmoil in their life, loss of continuity is one of the most unsettling things one can experience. Listen to “Strangers” below: Formed during the long winter of 2021, Agatha is Dead! began as a collaboration between Lilly and Noah, building songs in isolation before bringing them into the open. Drawing from the stark emotional landscape of Joy Division and the nocturnal melancholy of The Cure, the band’s sound merges restraint with intensity — a tension that has become central to their live presence. Joined by Joey Ramone Hansen on drums and Arthur on bass, the group quickly established itself within Berlin’s live circuit. Since signing to Duchess Box Records in 2025, Agatha is Dead! have built a reputation for performances that feel both intimate and unsettling. Following showcase appearances at SXSW, the band returned to Berlin for a sold-out headline show at Lido, confirming a growing presence beyond the city’s underground. With Concrete on the horizon, they now move into a wider run of German and European dates, including Reeperbahn Festival and their largest headline show to date at SO36 in Berlin on 25 February 2027. With “Strangers,” Agatha is Dead! step further into a world of dislocation and unease, where the familiar no longer offers comfort and what we once knew begins to blur. Agatha is Dead! items.body: Gabriele Poso has been releasing music since 2008, through Yoruba Records, BBE, Soundway, Wonderwheel and Mr. Bongo. For his sixth album he started his own imprint, AG Records, and recorded Maraviglia live to tape with a full band in an analogue studio in southern Italy. “Contigo Mi Vida” is the second single from the album, out on 19 June. Emanuele Coluccia leads on horns, moving between saxophone, flute and trumpet over Afro-Cuban percussion and a groove rooted in late-’70s Italian disco and Afrobeat. Maraviglia also features Andrea Rossetti on piano, Fender Rhodes, Hammond and Moog, Davide Codazzo on bass, Antonio De Donno on drums and percussion and Alberto Zacà on guitar. items.body: Review by The Progolyte — Not counting the various archival releases I've covered before, Malibran's sophomore album, Le Porte Del Silenzio, will be the first review I publish of an album recorded and released in the nineties. When it comes to Rock Progressivo Italiano overall, I haven't quite touched this era of the genre as I should have. Beyond these guys I really only know Nuova Era and D.F.A., so I still have some exploring to do here. Moving on, I would say this is a really strong retro Italian prog record, utilizing predominantly instrumental passages to exercise a very powerful and melodic style of progressive rock. One thing I wish was changed were some of the English lyrics, which sort of breaks the overall flow, as Italian ones would've fit the music better. Beyond that, this album is still very consistent and full of interesting symphonic prog with tons of neat little details and material to dig your teeth into, all within the grips of a very captivating album cover that seems to recall greatly to the work of Roger Dean with his art for Yes, specifically the cover of Relayer. The music here is very strong, fusing both keyboard and rhythm-driven progressive rock with thoroughly put-together neo-prog. It stays steady musically, not really losing my interest and always making for a fun experience. At some points it feels like the band can meander in this format for a while and just blend everything in together, which can feel a little too straightforward, but overall, there is some really nice material on here. The majority of the songs are ten minutes or under, with my favorites of these being the opening Livin' Alone and the driving Libero, which each seem to have more energy put into them and have the most satisfying moments in terms of technicality. That would be the case if it weren't for the monstrous ending to the album, the twenty-seven-minute-long title track, which is easily my favorite piece on the record. It's very emotionally charged but not sacrificing pure energy and chaos, where on most of the songs it seems to be fused together, this one keeps the sections more separate, distinct, and memorable. In conclusion, I would say this is a very fine example of retro Rock Progressivo Italiano and does a nice take on the classic sound while still sounding modern. Maybe not an essential as a whole, but seriously underrated in terms of exposure and definitely worth checking out if you want to get into more recent Italian prog. I'll be rewarding this one a strong 4/5.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张1993年发行的意大利复古前卫摇滚（Rock Progressivo Italiano）专辑，延续了七十年代意大利前卫摇滚的经典风格，融合了键盘主导的交响化编曲与新前卫摇滚的节奏感。专辑以器乐段落为主，旋律性强且编曲细腻，封面向Yes乐队《Relayer》致敬。亮点在于长达二十七分钟的同名终曲，情感张力与能量并存，段落对比清晰。整体而言，这是一张扎实且一致的复古意产前卫作品，但在创新性和跨领域融合方面较为保守，未涉及实验、爵士、电子或暗潮等元素，对偏好实验性与跨界融合的听众而言实验性不足，但仍保留了前卫摇滚的核心品质。

items.body: Norwegian darkwave and cyberpunk duo Rule of Two have released a cover of Depeche Mode’s “It’s No Good“. The Rule of Two “It’s No Good” version is accompanied by an official music video directed by band member Kristian Liljan. The cover is Rule of Two’s fifth single of 2026, following “Afterlife” via Polypiel Records on May 7 and “All Time Low” in February. ‘It’s No Good’: the original “It’s No Good” was released on March 31, 1997, as the second single from Depeche Mode’s ninth studio album “Ultra” (Mute Records, April 14, 1997). The track was written by Martin Gore and produced by Tim Simenon, recorded at Eastcote Studios in London and Larrabee West in Los Angeles, and mixed at Abbey Road Studios. It reached number five in the United Kingdom and number one in Denmark, Spain, Sweden and on the US Billboard Dance Club Play chart. About Rule of Two Rule of Two is a darkwave and cyberpunk duo formed in Oslo, Norway, in 2023 by Ronny Flissundet and Kristian Liljan, both from the Oslo metal and alternative rock underground with prior activity in Damokles, Dunderbeist and Kite. The project blends eerie synthesizers, mechanical rhythms and glitch textures into a sound the duo describes as taking a darker, more industrial direction with each release. Their debut album “Aiming for the Sun” was announced by Side-Line in November 2025. The “It’s No Good” cover, out June 4, 2026, is their first cover of a Depeche Mode track.

items.body: Montréal-based darkwave and dark synthwave producer Das Mörtal has released the double single “Parasite & Ghost” via Lisbon Lux Records. The release also serves as a preview of the forthcoming mini-album “DECVY I,” scheduled for October 29, 2026, on the same label. The double single pairs two tracks that occupy distinct stylistic territory. “Parasite” is described as a fast-paced darkwave track about illness. Regarding the track, Das Mörtal says: “An illness has affected my body for some time now, and Parasite was made under a pain that I can’t quite shake off.” “Ghost” is a witch-house-infused pop single, with catchy vocal melodies and driving kick drum-infused percussion. Alongside the double single, Das Mörtal has announced “DECVY I,” a mini-album due October 29, 2026, via Lisbon Lux Records. About Das Mörtal Das Mörtal is the project of Cristobal Cortes, a Santiago, Chile-born producer who grew up in Montréal. His musical journey began in Berlin, where he relocated roughly a decade and a half ago seeking electronic music with a more aggressive, punk-oriented edge than the minimalist house and techno sound that dominated the Montréal scene at the time. In Berlin, Cortes encountered the DJ culture of clubs associated with Ellen Allien’s BPitch Control label, an experience that informed his understanding of dancefloor dynamics and formed his subsequent production approach. Back in Montréal, Cortes developed the Das Mörtal project and found a label home in Lisbon Lux Records, a Montréal-based imprint that helped disseminate his music internationally. His debut album “Always Loved” was followed by further EPs and singles, and his catalogue expanded to include the full-length “Bury To Sorrow” (October 2023), a twelve-track record featuring a collaboration with Dance With the Dead. An instrumental version of the album was released in May 2024. His most recent work before the current release was the EP “Origins” (October 17, 2025), which included the single “Falsche Daten” ORIGINS EP by Das Mörtal And now there is the double single “Parasite & Ghost”. “DECVY I” follows on October 29, 2026, on the same label.
items._cn_summary: Das Mörtal是来自蒙特利尔的暗潮与暗黑合成器制作人，出生于智利圣地亚哥。这张双单曲《Parasite & Ghost》收录两首风格各异的作品：《Parasite》为快节奏暗潮，主题围绕病痛与身体折磨；《Ghost》融合巫毒浩室元素，旋律朗朗上口，鼓点强劲。整体定位偏向舞曲化的暗潮流行，而非极端实验路线。音乐人曾旅居柏林，深受BPitch Control厂牌俱乐部文化影响，制作理念注重舞池动态。发行厂牌Lisbon Lux Records为蒙特利尔独立厂牌，后续迷你专辑《DECVY I》将于2026年10月推出。该作品在暗潮框架内融入流行旋律与巫毒浩室质感，对偏好实验与前卫声响的听众而言，创新性较为有限。
